BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r1.claim: The opening am is disconnected, equivalent to bal plus a hamza; al-Taysīr says that without a preceding interrogative alif it is a direct denial, asking whether they were witnesses and answering that they were not present.

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r2.claim: Jacob’s ‘coming of death’ means its signs, causes, and nearness, not the instant of death itself.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r2.anchor: إماراته وأسبابه وقرب خروجه من الدنيا

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r3.claim: The verse answers Jews who claimed Jacob instructed his sons to follow Judaism at death: they were absent, and Jacob in fact urged Islam.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r3.anchor: نزلت حين قالت اليهود للنبي عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r4.claim: Jacob asked what his sons would worship after him to reaffirm their monotheism and Islam and secure their pledge to remain steadfast.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r4.anchor: أي شيء تعبدونه بعد موتي أراد به تقريرهم على التوحيد

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib says the question covers more than formal worship: every act should seek God’s face and pleasure, avoiding whatever does not lead to Him; Jacob feared worldly distraction more than idols.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r5.anchor: قال الراغب لم يعن بقوله : ما تعبدون من بعدي العبادة المشروعة فقط

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r6.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r6.claim: The Mathnawī teaches that worldly possessions distract from God; the problem is heedlessness, not fabric, silver, or the number and weight of children themselves.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r6.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : يست دنيا از خدا غافل شدن

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r7.speaker: التفتازاني
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r7.claim: Al-Taftāzānī says mā can refer to rational or nonrational things while they are unspecified; once rationality is known, man is used for the rational and mā for other things.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r7.anchor: قال النحرير التفتازاني : وما عام أي

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r8.claim: The sons say they will worship the one God worshipped by their forefathers, acknowledged in existence, divinity, and entitlement to worship; Ishmael, though Jacob’s uncle, is included as a father because an uncle is like a father.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r8.anchor: نعبد الإله المتفق على وجوده وإلهيته ووجوب عبادته

BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r9.claim: The Prophet compares a man’s paternal uncle to his father’s twin, just as two palm shoots are paired.
BURSEVI:v1p191#2/r9.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : "عم الرجل صنو أبيه

BURSEVI:v1p192/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p192/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p192/r1.claim: ‘One God’ is either an appositive to the God of the forefathers or an expression of specification; it states monotheism and removes ambiguity from repeating the possessive.
BURSEVI:v1p192/r1.anchor: بدل من إله آبائك وفائدته التصريح بالتوحيد ودفع التوهم الناشىء من تكرار المضاف

BURSEVI:v1p192/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p192/r2.claim: ‘We submit to Him’ is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ‘we worship.’

BURSEVI:v1p192/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p192/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p192/r3.claim: ‘That community’ points to Abraham, Jacob, and their monotheistic descendants; umma first means an intended goal and then a group people aim at and follow.
BURSEVI:v1p192/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى الأمة المذكورة التي هي إبراهيم ويعقوب وبنوهما الموحدون

BURSEVI:v1p192/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p192/r4.claim: The community ‘passed away’ by dying and became separate from others; the expression derives from becoming empty or uninhabited.
BURSEVI:v1p192/r4.anchor: مضت بالموت وانفردت عمن عداها وأصله صارت إلى الخلاء

QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r9.claim: Jacob’s family followed one path of monotheism and submission, inherited generation after generation, and were God’s purified people of nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r9.anchor: جروا كلهم - صلوات الله عليهم - على منهاج واحد في التوحيد والإسلام

QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r10.claim: The sons say “your God” rather than “our God” to honor Jacob’s distinction and their own lower station, then attest that they submit to God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r10.anchor: حيث سلموا له المزية ، ورأوا أنفسهم ملحقين بمقامه

QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r11.claim: God assigns each person and group a fitting rank and measure; each has its own sphere and its own share of felicity.
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r11.anchor: وأفرد لكل واحد قدرا بموجب حكمه

AKHFASH:v1p158/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p158/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p158/r3.claim: أم كنتم شهداء is an independent question.

AKHFASH:v1p158/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p158/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p158/r4.claim: The second إذ in إذ قال لبنيه is an appositive explaining the first إذ.
AKHFASH:v1p158/r4.anchor: وقال {إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه} فأبدل "إذ" الاخرة من الأولى

AKHFASH:v1p158/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p158/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p158/r5.claim: إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق are appositives in the genitive after آبائك; being foreign names, they do not decline.
AKHFASH:v1p158/r5.anchor: وقال {الهك واله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق} على البدل وهو في موضع جر إلا أنها [65ب] أعجمية فلا تنصرف

AKHFASH:v1p158#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p158#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p158#2/r1.claim: إلها واحدا is accusative as a circumstantial expression (ḥāl).

MAJAZ:v1p56/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p56/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p56/r4.claim: أم after a completed statement is a new alternative or correction, not the interrogatives هل or hamza; al-Akhṭal's verse illustrates this.
MAJAZ:v1p56/r4.anchor: «أم» تجيء بعد كلام قد انقطع، وليست في موضع هل

MAJAZ:v1p56/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p56/r5.speaker: الأخطل
MAJAZ:v1p56/r5.claim: Al-Akhṭal's verse exemplifies أم following a statement that has ended; it can be paraphrased “did you see?” or “rather, you saw.”
MAJAZ:v1p56/r5.anchor: قال الأخطل: كذبتك عينك أم رأيت بواسط ... غلس الظلام

MAJAZ:v1p56/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p56/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p56/r6.claim: Arabic can call a paternal or maternal uncle a father.

MAJAZ:v1p56/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p56/r7.speaker: عكرمة
MAJAZ:v1p56/r7.claim: A report about the Prophet at the conquest says he feared Quraysh might treat his father as Thaqīf had treated ʿUrwa; the Prophet had sent ʿUrwa to invite Thaqīf to Islam, where he was killed.
MAJAZ:v1p56/r7.anchor: قال حماد بن زيد عن أيوب، عن عكرمة: إن النبي

NAHHAS:v1p264/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r7.claim: شهداء is the predicate of كان and is diptote because its plural feminine ending marks the group, like a feminine hāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r7.anchor: خبر كان ولم يصرفه لأن فيه ألف التأنيث ودخلت لتأنيث الجماعة

NAHHAS:v1p264/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r8.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p264/r8.claim: Sibawayh says fronting يعقوب before الموت emphasizes the item whose explanation matters more to the speakers.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r8.anchor: مفعول مقدم وفي تقديمه فائدة على مذهب سيبويه

NAHHAS:v1p264/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r9.claim: ما in ما تعبدون is the accusative object of تعبدون.

NAHHAS:v1p264/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r10.claim: Ibrahim, Ismail, and Ishaq are genitive appositives to آبائك and remain diptote as foreign names.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r10.anchor: إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ) في موضع خفض على البدل ولم تصرف لأنها أعجمية

NAHHAS:v1p264/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r11.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p264/r11.claim: Al-Kisaʾi permits full declension for Ishaq if derived from سحق, and for Yaʿqub if transferred from an Arabic word.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r11.anchor: قال الكسائي إن شئت صرفت إسحاقا وجعلته من السحق وصرفت يعقوب

NAHHAS:v1p264/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r12.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects the rationale for reading إله أبيك as singular: Arabs call an uncle father, and the resulting coordination awkwardly separates Ishaq, the nearer father.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r12.anchor: هذا لا يجب لأن العرب تسمى العم أبا وأيضا فإن هذا بعيد

NAHHAS:v1p264/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r13.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p264/r13.claim: A second analysis treats أبيك as a plural, supported by Sibawayh’s forms أبون and أبين and the verse فقلنا أسلموا إنا أخوكم.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r13.anchor: على مذهب سيبويه يكون أبيك جمعا حكى سيبويه أبون وأبين

NAHHAS:v1p264/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r14.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
NAHHAS:v1p264/r14.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalil give the plurals براهيم and سماعيل for Ibrahim and Ismail.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r14.anchor: سيبويه والخليل يقولان في جمع إبراهيم وإسماعيل براهيم وسماعيل

NAHHAS:v1p264/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r15.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p264/r15.claim: The Kufans also report براهمة and سماعلة, with hāʾ replacing yāʾ as in زنادقة, and the shorter براهم and سماعل.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r15.anchor: وحكوا أيضا براهمة وسماعلة والهاء بدل من الياء كما يقال زنادقة

NAHHAS:v1p264/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r16.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v1p264/r16.claim: Ibn Yazid rejects adding hamza in these plural forms and proposes أباره and أسامع, also allowing أبارِيه and أساميع.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r16.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد هذا غلط لأن الهمزة ليس هذا موضع زيادتها ولكن أقول أباره وأسامع

NAHHAS:v1p264/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r17.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
NAHHAS:v1p264/r17.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya allows براه by analogy with the diminutive بريه; the source also lists plural variants for Ishaq and Yaʿqub.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r17.anchor: وأجاز أحمد بن يحيى براه كما يقال في التصغير بريه وجمع إسحاق أساحيق

NAHHAS:v1p264/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r18.claim: The regular sound masculine plurals Ibrahimun, Ishaqūn, Ismailūn, and Yaʿqubūn are the standard pattern, since that plural leaves the stem unchanged.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r18.anchor: والباب في هذا كله أن يجمع مسلما فيقال إبراهيمون وإسحاقون وإسماعيلون ويعقوبون

NAHHAS:v1p264/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r19.claim: إلها واحدا is accusative either as a circumstantial phrase or apposition; indefinite and definite nouns may replace one another in apposition.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r19.anchor: إلها واحدا ) نصب على الحال وإن شئت على البدل لأنه يجوز أن تبدل النكرة من المعرفة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r1.claim: The question about witnessing Jacob’s death is addressed to the People of the Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية قوله : أم كنتم شهداء يعني اهل الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r2.claim: No Jews, Christians, or other people witnessed Jacob’s deathbed covenant requiring his sons to worship only God; the sons affirmed it and their Islam was attested.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قوله : أم كنتم شهداء اذ حضر يعقوب الموت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r3.claim: Their answer that they would worship means that they would affirm God’s oneness.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : نعبد يعني نوحد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r4.claim: The word jadd means grandfather, as Ibn ʿAbbas illustrates by reciting the verse’s list of ancestors.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r4.anchor: عن عمرو عن عطاء قال : سمعت ابن عباس يقول : الجد اب ويتلوا ابن عباس : قالوا نعبد الهك واله ابائك

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r5.claim: Jacob called his uncle his father when listing Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية : اذ حضر يعقوب الموت اذ قال لبنيه ما تعبدون من بعدي قالوا نعبد الهك واله ابائك إبراهيم واسماعيل واسحاق فسمى عمه اباه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r6.claim: A maternal uncle and a paternal uncle are both called father.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r6.anchor: سمعت محمد بن كعب يقول : الخال والد والعم والد ،

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r7.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r7.claim: The one God is the deity of everything and creator of everything.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r7.anchor: عن عطاء الها واحدا قال : انه اله واحد واله كل شئ ، وخالق كل شئ

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r8.claim: Their being Muslims means that they affirm God’s oneness.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#3/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس مسلمين يقول : موحدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r1.claim: Their response naʿbudu is the answer completing Jacob's question, not an independent sentence; dialogue therefore omits the conjunction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r1.anchor: جاءت على طريقة المحاورات بدون واو وليست استئنافا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r2.claim: Calling God your god rather than using the proper name invokes the attributes Jacob and the forefathers taught and signals the sons' imitation of them amid surrounding idolaters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r2.anchor: إضافة إله إلى ضمير يعقوب وإلى آبائه تفيد جميع الصفات التي كان يعقوب وآباؤه يصفون الله بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r3.claim: The added names Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac form a rhetorical list honoring the ancestors, comparable to Rabiʿa ibn Naṣr ibn Quʿayn's genealogical verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r3.anchor: إن يقتلوك فقد ثللت عروشهم بعتيبة بن الحارث بن شهاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r4.claim: Repeating ilāh before the coordinated fathers is more eloquent but not obligatory; fathers includes Jacob's uncle Ishmael by kinship inclusion because an uncle is like a father.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r4.anchor: لأن إعادة المضاف مع المعطوف على المضاف إليه أفصح في الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r5.claim: Isaac was Abraham's son by Sarah, younger than Ishmael by fourteen years, and ancestor of Israelites and related peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r5.anchor: وأما إسحاق فهو ابن إبراهيم وهو أصغر من إسماعيل بأربع عشرة سنة وأمه سارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r6.claim: Jews say Isaac was the son Abraham was commanded to sacrifice; Ibn ʿAshur insists it was Ishmael, Abraham's only son at the time, and notes the Torah calls the son unique although Isaac was never an only child.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p733/r6.anchor: إن الابن الذي أمر الله إبراهيم بذبحه وفداه الله هو إسحاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r1.claim: In ilāhan wāḥidan, ilāhan is a circumstantial qualifier of ilāhuka, while wāḥidan carries the actual description; repeating the noun clarifies and incidentally reinforces it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r2.claim: Repeating a word before a new predicate or complement is eloquent when the repeated material adds information, as in the cited Qur'anic verses and al-Aḥwaṣ al-Anṣārī's line.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r2.anchor: وإنما أعيد لفظ إلاها ولم يقتصر على وصف واحدا لزيادة الإيضاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r3.speaker: ابن جني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r3.claim: Ibn Jinni says saying iza qumt qumt is pointless, but the poetic repetition works because the second verb takes a preposition that contributes new meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r3.anchor: قال ابن جني في ( شرح الحماسة ) محال أن تقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers two alternatives: apposition of a qualified indefinite to a definite, or an accusative of specification with an implied command to praise; Ibn ʿAshur favors his own analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734/r4.anchor: وجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) أن يكون قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734#2/r1.claim: Wa-naḥnu lahu muslimūn is either a circumstantial clause tied to the subject of worship or coordinated with it; its nominal form expresses lasting submission, while the verb expresses renewal and continuity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p734#2/r1.anchor: جملة في موضع الحال من ضمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.claim: The address rebukes Jews and Christians claiming the prophets for their own religions: Jacob and the earlier prophets followed pure monotheism and submission, so the claimants lack eyewitness knowledge and are inventing their claim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.anchor: هذا الخطاب لليهود والنصارى الذين انتحلوا الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.claim: Some take am as “rather”: the ancestors witnessed Jacob and learned his testament but rejected it and falsely attributed another religion to him; Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds “rather” plus an interrogative hamza the strongest reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.anchor: والأظهر أنها التي بمعنى بل وألف الاستفهام معا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says am can pose a question in the middle of discourse after an earlier opening, as in examples such as “Or do they say he invented it?”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.anchor: وحكى الطبري أن أم يستفهم بها في وسط كلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.claim: Shuhadāʾ means witnesses who were present; Jacob's “death came” means its preliminaries, since a person at the instant of death could not speak. Jacob is placed first because he is the focus; the second id-clause apposes the first.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.anchor: لو حضر الموت لما أمكن أن يقول شيئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.claim: Jacob asks what they will worship as a test; using “what” rather than “whom” avoids opening a path to their claim, and common objects of worship include idols, fire, sun, and stones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.anchor: ولم يقل من لئلا يطرق لهم الاهتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.claim: A report says Jacob chose death, asked for time to advise his family, and gathered his sons, who affirmed their faith and knowledge of God; “after me” means after his death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.anchor: وقال أمهلوني حتى أوصي بني وأهلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.claim: Ismāʿīl is included among Jacob's fathers because he was his uncle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.anchor: ودخل إسماعيل في الآباء لأنه عم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: The Prophet asked that al-ʿAbbās be returned to him, fearing Quraysh would treat him as Thaqīf had treated ʿUrwa b. Masʿūd; elsewhere he called him a remnant of his forefathers and said “I am the son of the two sacrificed,” on the well-known view that Isaac was the sacrifice.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r2.claim: They read “and the god of your father” in the singular; it may mean Abraham alone, though some parse abī as a sound masculine plural, attested by Sībawayh and Ziyād b. Wāṣil's verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء «وإله أبيك»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ismāʿīl is named before Isaac because he was older.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r3.anchor: يقال قدم إسماعيل لأنه أسن من إسحاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p214/r4.claim: Ilāhan may be an appositive repeating “your God” to add the quality of oneness, or a circumstantial accusative; Ibn ʿAṭiyya favors the latter because the point is to establish the state of unity. “We submit to Him” is more laudatory as a complete clause than as a circumstantial phrase.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after Jews told the Prophet that Jacob had instructed his sons to follow Judaism when he died.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149#2/r1.anchor: سبب نزولها أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألست تعلم أن يعقوب أوصى بنيه يوم مات باليهودية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r1.claim: Jacob's deathbed instruction argues against Arab polytheists descended from Ismail and Israelite disbelievers: he charged his sons to worship God alone; Ismail is included as their father by rhetorical predominance although he was their uncle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r1.anchor: وهذا من باب التغليب لأن إسماعيل عمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r2.speaker: النحاس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r2.claim: Al-Nahhas says Arabs call an uncle a father; al-Qurtubi transmits the point.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r2.anchor: قال النحاس: والعرب تسمي العم أبا، نقله القرطبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r3.claim: Some use this verse to support the grandfather as a father who blocks siblings from inheritance; al-Bukhari transmits this as Abu Bakr's view through Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, without disagreement reported from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r3.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية من جعل الجد أبا وحجب به الإخوة، كما هو قول الصديق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r4.speaker: عائشة والحسن البصري وطاوس وعطاء وأبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r4.claim: They, along with many early and later scholars, hold that the grandfather takes the position of a father and excludes siblings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r4.anchor: وإليه ذهبت عائشة أم المؤمنين، وبه يقول الحسن البصري وطاوس وعطاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r5.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r5.claim: Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad according to his well-known position hold that the grandfather shares inheritance with siblings; Malik attributes this view to several Companions and others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r5.anchor: وقال مالك والشافعي وأحمد في المشهور عنه أنه يقاسم الإخوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد بن الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, chose the view that the grandfather excludes siblings; Ibn Kathir says fuller evidence is discussed elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447/r6.anchor: واختاره صاحبا أبي حنيفة القاضي: أبو يوسف، ومحمد بن الحسن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447#2/r1.claim: 'One God' means that they affirm His sole divinity and associate nothing with Him; 'submitted' means obedient and humble. Islam is the religion of every prophet despite differing laws and paths, as in 3:83 and 21:25 and the hadith that the prophets share one religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p447#2/r1.anchor: أي: نوحده بالألوهية، ولا نشرك به شيئا غيره {ونحن له مسلمون} أي: مطيعون خاضعون

SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r1.claim: The famous analysis makes أم disconnected, equivalent to بل plus an interrogative: it shifts topic without cancellation, and the reproachful question implies denial, meaning they were not witnesses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r1.anchor: أنها منقطعة، والمنقطعة تقدر ب " بل " وهمزة الاستفهام وبعضهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says أم means an interrogative alif at the beginning of speech in a Yemeni dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r2.anchor: قال: " وأم تكون بمعنى ألف الاستفهام في صدر الكلام، لغة يمانية "

SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r3.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r3.claim: Al-Tabari treats أم as a question particle used in the middle of speech whose opening has already occurred.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r3.anchor: وقال الطبري: " إن أم يستفهم بها وسط كلام قد تقدم صدره "

SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r4.claim: The Sheikh says he knows no grammarian supporting Ibn Atiyya's dialect analysis and calls al-Tabari's account unusual.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r4.anchor: لم أقف لأحد من النحويين على ما قال

SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r5.claim: Zamakhshari also proposes connected أم, addressing Jews who claimed the prophets died as Jews; he supplies an omitted prior question about their accusation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r5.anchor: ولكن الوجه أن تكون " أم " متصلة على أن يقدر قبلها محذوف كأنه قيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r6.claim: The Sheikh rejects the connected reading's omitted coordinated clause: grammarians do not permit such deletion, apart from limited cases with conjunctions and clear evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا أعلم أحدا أجاز حذف هذه الجملة، لا يحفظ ذلك في شعر ولا غيره

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r1.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r1.claim: Deleting the counterpart بعد الحر in تقيكم الحر is licensed because a positive question entails its negative counterpart; poetic examples also show rare deletion after أو and حتى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r1.anchor: وإنما جاز ذلك لأن المستفهم عن الإثبات يتضمن نقيضه، ويجوز حذف الثواني المقابلات

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r2.claim: شهداء is the predicate of كان and may mean witnesses or martyrs.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r2.anchor: و " شهداء " خبر كان وهو جمع شاهد أو شهيد، وقد تقدم أول السورة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r3.claim: إذ حضر is a time adverb governed by شهداء, not its object; death's arrival is a metonym for its causes and preliminaries, as a poet says أنا الموت for its cause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r3.anchor: أي: شهداء وقت حضور الموت إياه، وحضور الموت كناية عن حضور أسبابه ومقدماته

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r4.claim: The common reading makes يعقوب accusative and الموت nominative, fronting the object for emphasis; some reverse the cases.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r4.anchor: والمشهور نصب " يعقوب " ورفع " الموت " ، قدم المفعول اهتماما

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r5.claim: Some read حضر with kasra on ḍād, although its present with ḍamma is irregular, perhaps from blending two patterns.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#2/r5.anchor: والمضارع يحضر بالضم شاذ، وكأنه من التداخل وقد تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r1.claim: The second إذ قال may be apposition to the first إذ, with its governor determined by whether apposition repeats the governor, or a time adverb of حضر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r1.anchor: " إذ " هذه فيها قولان أحدهما: بدل من الأولى، والعامل فيها:

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r2.claim: ما تعبدون is an interrogative object placed first because interrogatives occupy the sentence opening; من بعدي means after my death.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r2.anchor: وهو واجب التقديم لأن له صدر الكلام وأتى ب " ما " دون

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r3.claim: ما may ask about an object's quality, like asking whether Zayd is a jurist or physician; alternatively the objects were nonrational idols or celestial bodies.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " كما تقول: ما زيد؟ تريد: أفقيه أم طبيب أم غير ذلك من الصفات

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r4.claim: ما may describe an unknown object; another proposed reason is that Jacob tested his sons without prompting them toward the answer, unlike من for rational beings.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#3/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أن " ما " للمبهم أمره، فإذا علم فرق ب " ما " و " من

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r1.claim: The repeated إله before آبائك avoids coordinating with a genitive pronoun without repeating its preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r1.anchor: أعاد ذكر الإله لئلا يعطف على الضمير المجرور دون إعادة الجار

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r2.speaker: الحسن ويحيى وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r2.claim: They read أبيك instead of آبائك; Ubayy reads وإله إبراهيم, omitting the ancestor word.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويحيى وأبو رجاء " أبيك " ، وقرأ أبي: " وإله إبراهيم " فأسقط

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r3.claim: On the common reading إبراهيم وما بعده may be apposition or explanatory apposition, or accusative with omitted أعني; the inflection also shows grandfather and uncle can be called father.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r3.anchor: وفي " إبراهيم " وما بعده حينئذ ثلاثة أوجه، أوحدها: أنه بدل

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r4.claim: Some call naming Abraham and Ishmael fathers an instance of predominance of الأب; the author objects that singular usage also occurs where no coordination permits such predominance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم: " وهذا من باب التغليب، يعني أنه غلب الأب على غيره

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r5.claim: أبيك may be literal singular or a plural used in its place; alternatively it is sound plural أبين with its nūn dropped in annexation, supported by Sibawayh and two poetic lines.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r5.anchor: الثاني: يكون جمع سلامة بالياء والنون، وإنما حذفت النون للإضافة

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r6.claim: إسحاق is a foreign proper name and indeclinable, but as an Arabic verbal noun from أسحق it would decline; its plurals include أساحقة and أساحيق.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#4/r6.anchor: وإسحاق علم أعجمي ويكون مصدر أسحق

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r1.claim: إلها واحدا may be an appositive to إلهك, either an indefinite modified noun as in 96:15 or an unmodified indefinite appositive accepted by Basrans.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه بدل من " إلهك " بدل نكرة موصوفة من معرفة كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r2.claim: It may instead be a circumstantial from إلهك, governed by نعبد; both this and apposition emphasize one deity because annexation can suggest multiplicity, and the circumstantial is موطئة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r2.anchor: وفائدة البدل والحال التنصيص على أن معبودهم فرد إذ إضافة الشيء إلى كثير

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r3.claim: Zamakhshari parses إلها واحدا as an accusative of specification, meaning they intend the one God as one deity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r3.anchor: الثالث: - وإليه نحا الزمخشري - أن يكون منصوبا على الاختصاص

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r4.claim: The Sheikh objects that grammarians do not allow specification to be indefinite or ambiguous.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#5/r4.anchor: وقد نص النحويون على أن المنصوب على الاختصاص لا يكون نكرة

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r1.claim: ونحن له مسلمون may coordinate with نعبد as an expanded answer, or be a circumstantial clause whose governor is نعبد.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها معطوفة على قوله: " نعبد " يعني أنها تتمة جوابهم له

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r2.claim: Zamakhshari says the clause has no syntactic position and is parenthetical emphasis: their state is one of sincere submission.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r2.anchor: والثالث: - وإليه نحا الزمخشري - ألا يكون لها محل، بل هي جملة اعتراضية مؤكدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r3.claim: The Sheikh says a parenthesis strengthens two linked parts spoken by the same speaker; here Jacob's sons speak before it, but God reports about them after it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r3.anchor: ما قبلها من مقول بني يعقوب وما بعدها من كلام الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls it a new subject and predicate, meaning they were and will be in that state; the Sheikh sees no need to posit an omitted coordinated clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:133#6/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ونحن له مسلمون ابتداء وخبر أي: كذلك كنا ونحن نكون "

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r1.claim: Am is disconnected and rebuking; shahīd means present, and believers did not witness Jacob’s death but know it by revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r1.anchor: الشهداء جمع شهيد ، بمعنى الحاضر : أي ما كنتم حاضرين يعقوب عليه السلام إذ حضره الموت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r2.claim: Another view addresses Jews, who claimed prophets died as Jews; witnessing Jacob’s demand for Islam would have exposed that claim.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r2.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب لليهود ، لأنهم كانوا يقولون : ما مات نبي إلا على اليهودية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r3.claim: Because the disconnected reading fits Jews poorly, he prefers a connected question with an implied charge: were they alleging prophets were Jews? Their ancestors witnessed Jacob demand monotheism.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r3.anchor: ولكن الوجه ان تكون متصلة على ان يقدر قبلها محذوف كانه قيل أتدعون على الأنبياء اليهودية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r4.claim: A dialect pronounces ḥaḍara with kasra on the ḍād.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p218/r4.anchor: وقرىء ( حضر ) بكسر الضاد وهي لغة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r1.claim: Mā is general, unlike man, which scholars use for rational beings; ‘whom do you worship?’ would exclude other objects of worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r1.anchor: عام في كل شيء فإذا علم فرق بما ومن وكفاك دليلا قول العلماء ( من ) لما يعقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r2.claim: Mā taʿbudūn can ask about the worshipped being’s attributes, as ‘What is Zayd?’ asks whether he is a jurist or physician.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r2.anchor: سؤال عن صفة المعبود كما تقول ما زيد تريد أفقيه أم طبيب أم غير ذلك من الصفات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r3.claim: Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac explain ‘your fathers’; Ishmael’s inclusion, though he was Jacob’s uncle, is known through revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r3.anchor: عطف بيان لآبائك وجعل إسماعيل وهو عمه من طريق الوحي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: He again favors an implied accusation and connected am when Jews are addressed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: فالآية منافية لقولهم فكيف يقال لهم ( أم كنتم شهداء ) ولكن الوجه ان تكون أم متصلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.claim: Mā asks generally what is worshipped, unlike man, restricted to rational beings; it can also ask about the object’s quality.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r1.anchor: عام في كل شيء فإذا علم فرق بما ومن وكفاك دليلا قول العلماء ( من ) لما يعقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.claim: Ishmael, Jacob’s uncle, is counted among his forefathers because an uncle is like a father and an aunt like a mother, as siblings have equal standing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r2.anchor: وجعل إسماعيل وهو عمه من جملة آبائه لأن العم أب والخالة أم لانخراطهما في سلك واحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.claim: The Prophet compares a paternal uncle to a father’s peer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r3.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه السلام 58 ( عم الرجل صنو أبيه )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.claim: A saying about al-ʿAbbās calls him the remnant of the Prophet’s forefathers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r4.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام في العباس 59 ( هذا بقية آبايك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.claim: The Prophet asks to bring his father, fearing Quraysh may treat him as Thaqīf treated ʿUrwa b. Masʿūd.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r5.anchor: 60 ( ردوا علي أبي فإني أخشى ان تفعل به قريش ما فعلت ثقيف بعروة بن مسعود )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.claim: Ubayy reads ‘and the god of Abraham,’ omitting ‘your fathers’; abīka may be singular with Abraham as apposition or a plural form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r6.anchor: بطرح آبائك وقرىء ( أبيك ) وفيه وجهان ان يكون واحدا وإبراهيم وحده عطف بيان له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.claim: An otherwise unnamed poetic line attests al-abīnā as a plural of father.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p219#2/r7.anchor: وان يكون جمعا بالواو والنون قال ( وفديننا بالأبينا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r1.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan is an appositional substitute for ‘the god of your fathers,’ like the Quranic construction ‘by the forelock, a lying forelock.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r1.anchor: أو على الاختصاص أي نريد بإلاه آبائك الها واحدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r2.claim: Alternatively it is specification: ‘we mean one god by the god of your fathers.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r2.anchor: أو على الاختصاص أي نريد بإلاه آبائك الها واحدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r3.claim: ‘We submit to Him’ may be a circumstantial clause attached to subject or object of ‘worship’; it may also coordinate or parenthetically affirm sincere monotheism and submission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p220/r3.anchor: حال من فاعل نعبد أو من مفعوله لرجوع الهاء اليه في له

MUQATIL:2:130-134/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:130-134/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:130-134/r4.claim: Against the Jews’ claim that Jacob left them Judaism, God says they did not witness his deathbed: Jacob asked whom his sons would worship, and they promised the one God of their forefathers.
MUQATIL:2:130-134/r4.anchor: وذلك أن اليهود قالوا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يا محمد، ألست تعلم أن يعقوب يوم مات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r1.claim: On the disconnected reading, the question denies that the believers witnessed Jacob's death; they know it only through revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r1.anchor: أو منقطعة ومعنى الهمزة فيها الإنكار والشهداء جمع شهيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r2.claim: Alternatively, the connected question addresses Jews who claimed every prophet died a Jew, challenging whether they witnessed Jacob's death.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r2.anchor: أو متصلة ويقدر قبلها محذوف والخطاب لليهود لأنهم كانوا يقولون ما مات نبى إلا على اليهودية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r3.claim: The second إذ either apposes the first or serves as an adverb for شهداء or حضر.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r3.anchor: يدل من إذ الأولى والعامل فيهما شهداء أو ظرف لحضر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r4.claim: Jacob asks generally what his sons worship after his death; ما may ask what thing or what attribute of the deity, like asking whether Zayd is a jurist or doctor.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r4.anchor: ما استفهام فى محل النصب بتعبدون أى أى شيء تعبدون وما عام فى كل شيء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r5.claim: They answer that they worship the God of their forefathers; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are appositional clarifications of forefathers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r5.anchor: عطف بيان لآبائك وجعل إسماعيل من جملة آبائه وهو عمه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: Ismāʿīl is included among Jacob's fathers because an uncle counts as a father; a report calls al-ʿAbbās the remainder of my fathers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: وجعل إسماعيل من جملة آبائه وهو عمه لأن العم اب قال عليه السلام فى العباس هذا بقية آبائى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r7.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan is either an appositive to the preceding deity or an accusative of specification meaning they intend one God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r7.anchor: بدل من إله آبائك كقوله بالناصية ناصية كاذبة أو نصب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r8.claim: We are Muslims is either a circumstantial clause, coordinated with worship, or parenthetical emphasis.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p72/r8.anchor: حال من فاعل نعبد أو جملة معطوفة على نعبد أو جملة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r1.claim: The address challenges Jews and Christians who attribute to Ibrahim a religion he did not prescribe: they did not witness Jacob's testament and are falsely claiming knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r1.anchor: والخطاب لليهود والنصارى الذين ينسبون إلى إبراهيم ما لم يوص به بنيه،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r2.claim: أم means بل, shifting to a reproachful question about whether their ancestors witnessed Jacob; شهداء is the predicate of كان and is a plural of شاهد.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r2.anchor: و «أم» بمعنى بل أي بل أشهد أسلافكم يعقوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r3.claim: The first إذ is governed by the sense of witnessing, and the second is appositional to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r3.anchor: والعامل في «إذ» الأولى معنى الشهادة، و «إذ» الثانية بدل من الأولى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r4.claim: Jacob's being overtaken by death means its preliminaries and causes, since a person actually at death could not speak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r4.anchor: ومعنى «حضر يعقوب الموت» أي مقدماته وأسبابه وإلا فلو حضر الموت لما أمكن أن يقول شيئا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r5.claim: The wording asks what they worship rather than whom to test what they would say; it also fits the customary inanimate objects worshipped besides God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r5.anchor: وعبر عن المعبود ب «ما»: ولم يقل من لأنه أراد أن يختبرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r6.claim: من بعدي means after my death.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r6.anchor: ومعنى «من بعدي» أي من بعد موتي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r7.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r7.claim: An account says Jacob, when given the prophets' choice, chose death but requested time to advise his family; his sons answered faithfully and affirmed knowledge of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r7.anchor: وحكي أن يعقوب حين خير كما تخير الأنبياء اختار الموت وقال: أمهلوني حتى أوصي بني وأهلي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r8.claim: Ibrahim, Ismail, and Isaac are genitive appositions and remain indeclinable because they are foreign names; al-Kisāʾī permits Arabic derivations that would make Isaac or Jacob declinable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r8.anchor: «إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحق» في موضع خفض على البدل، ولم تنصرف لأنها أعجمية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r9.claim: God calls both the uncle and grandfather a father, and names the grandfather before Ismail, the uncle, because Ismail was older than Isaac.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r9.anchor: وسمى الله كل واحد من العم والجد أبا، وبدأ بذكر الجد ثم إسماعيل العم لأنه أكبر من إسحق.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r10.claim: إلها is an indefinite apposition to إلهك, repeated to express God's oneness; it may instead be a circumstantial accusative, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers a good account of the intended affirmation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r10.anchor: و «إلها» بدل من «إلهك» بدل النكرة من المعرفة وكرره لفائدة الصفة بالوحدانية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r11.speaker: الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء العطاردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r11.claim: They read وإله أبيك; one explanation has the singular refer only to Ibrahim and avoids calling Ismail a father, though al-Naḥḥās says Arabs do call an uncle a father.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r11.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويحيى بن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء العطاردي «وإله أبيك»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r12.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r12.claim: A second explanation parses أبيك as a sound plural of أب, supported by poetic examples.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133/r12.anchor: على مذهب سيبويه أن يكون «أبيك» جمع سلامة حكى سيبويه أب وأبون وأبين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.claim: ونحن له مسلمون is a nominal clause or a circumstantial clause governed by نعبد.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.anchor: ونحن له مسلمون } ابتداء وخبر ويحتمل أن يكون في موضع الحال، والعامل «نعبد».

RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r1.claim: The account of Jacob’s testament follows Abraham’s to reinforce the proof against Jews and Christians and make the case clearer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r1.anchor: ذكر عقيبه أن يعقوب وصى بنيه بمثل ذلك تأكيدا للحجة على اليهود والنصارى

RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r2.claim: The particle am may be connected or disconnected: connected am asks which of two alternatives is true, while disconnected am means “rather” plus a question and abandons the prior assertion.
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r2.anchor: وأما المنقطعة فقالوا : إنها بمعنى ( بل ) مع همزة الاستفهام

RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r3.claim: The connected form asks which of two known alternatives applies; unlike the disconnected form, its second option stays linked to the first and can be restated as “which one?”
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r3.anchor: ولم يكن ( ما ) بعد ( أم ) منقطعا عما قبله بدليل أن عمرا قرين زيد

RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r4.claim: Qur’anic examples distinguish connected am in 79:27 from disconnected am in 32:1–3, where “rather, do they say he fabricated it?” rejects the prior assertion; treating it as a bare hamza is mistaken.
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r4.anchor: ومن لا يحقق من المفسرين يقولون إن ( أم ) ههنا بمنزلة الهمزة وذلك غير صحيح

RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r5.claim: “Witnesses” means people present; the address challenges the People of the Book, whose claim to follow the prophets conflicts with the prophets’ call to Islam and Muhammad’s same religion.
RAZI-FULL:v4p67/r5.anchor: ( والشهداء ) جمع شهيد بمعنى الحاضر أي ما كنتم حاضرين

RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r1.claim: On the disconnected reading, the rebuke targets only the false claim that the addressees were present at Jacob’s death; the quoted testament itself is true and is then explained.
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r1.anchor: الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار متعلق بمجرد ادعائهم الحضور عند وفاته

RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r2.claim: On the connected reading, an omitted question asks whether they claim the prophets were Jews or were present at Jacob’s death; Israel’s ancestors saw his call to Islam and monotheism.
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r2.anchor: القول الثاني : في أن ( أم ) في هذه الآية متصلة ، وطريق ذلك أن يقدر قبلها محذوف

RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r3.claim: Qaffal says the first “when” marks the time of the alleged witnesses, while the second marks the time Jacob was present at death.
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r3.anchor: قال القفال قوله : { إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه } أن ( إذ ) الأولى وقت الشهداء

RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r4.claim: The verse shows that the prophets’ solicitude for their children centered on religion.
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r4.anchor: الآية دالة على أن شفقة الأنبياء عليهم السلام على أولادهم كانت في باب الدين

RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r5.claim: The interrogative ma can be general—“what thing do you worship?”—or a request for definition, like asking “what is a human?”
RAZI-FULL:v4p68/r5.anchor: أن ( ما ) عام في كل شيء والمعنى أي شيء تعبدون

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r1.claim: Razi says the verse proves neither that Jacob’s sons knew God by rational argument nor that they accepted Him only through imitation and instruction.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r1.anchor: كما أنه ليس في الآية دلالة على أنهم عرفوا الإله بالدليل العقلي

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r2.claim: Since exclusive reliance on imitation or instruction is disproved, the sons’ faith must have been grounded in reasoning.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r2.anchor: ثم إن القول بالتقليد والتعليم لما بطل بالدليل علمنا أن إيمان القوم ما كان على هذه الطريقة

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r3.claim: The verse proves neither rational proof nor exclusive dependence on imitation and instruction; since those exclusive paths are disproved, the sons’ faith must rest on reasoning.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r3.anchor: فليس فيها أيضا دلالة على أنهم ما أقروا بالإله إلا على طريقة التقليد والتعليم

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r4.claim: They omitted a full exposition of God’s unity, knowledge, power, and justice for brevity.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r4.anchor: أن ذلك أخصر في القول من شرح صفات الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r5.claim: Their wording reassured Jacob that they followed his own path and would worship God alone without opposing him.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r5.anchor: لسنا نجري إلا على مثل طريقتك فلا خلاف منا عليك

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r6.claim: Their reference to the God of Jacob and the ancestors may point to the rational proof in 2:21: the creator demonstrated by their existence.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r6.anchor: وههنا مرادهم بقولهم : { نعبد إلاهك وإلاه آبائك } أي : نعبد الإله الذي دل عليه وجودك

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r7.claim: Qaffal relates that Jacob saw Egyptians worshipping fire and idols and questioned his sons out of fear for their faith.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r7.anchor: قال القفال : وفي بعض التفاسير أن يعقوب عليه السلام لما دخل مصر رأى أهلها

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r8.claim: The Qadi reports Ibn Abbas’s story that Jacob gathered his sons at death while they worshipped idols and fire and asked what they would worship after him.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r8.anchor: وحكى القاضي عن ابن عباس : أن يعقوب عليه السلام جمعهم إليه عند الوفاة

RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r9.claim: The Qadi calls that story unlikely: the sons’ prompt monotheistic answer implies settled knowledge, and the Qur’an describes Jacob’s descendants as righteous.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69/r9.anchor: هذا بعيد لوجهين . الأول : أنهم بادروا إلى الاعتراف بالتوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.claim: Qaffal treats Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac as an appositional explanation of “your fathers”; Ishmael precedes Isaac because he was older.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.anchor: قال القفال : وقيل أنه قدم ذكر إسماعيل على إسحاق لأن إسماعيل كان أسن من إسحاق

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.claim: Shafi‘i, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Mas‘ud, Zayd, Malik, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad hold that full or paternal siblings are not excluded from inheritance by a grandfather.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : الأخوة والأخوات للأب والأم أو للأب لا يسقطون بالجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa, Abu Bakr, Ibn Abbas, Aisha, and several Successors hold that a grandfather excludes siblings from inheritance.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : إنهم يسقطون بالجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r4.claim: Among those who do not let a grandfather exclude siblings, Zayd and Shafi‘i give him the better of sharing with them or one-third of the estate, then divide the remainder among siblings, males receiving twice females.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r4.anchor: أن الجد خير الأمرين : إما المقاسمة معهم أو ثلث جميع المال

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r5.claim: A second non-exclusion rule treats the grandfather as one of the siblings unless that would reduce his share below one-sixth, in which case he receives one-sixth.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r5.anchor: أنه بمنزلة أحد الأخوة ما لم تنقصه المقاسمة من السدس

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that this verse calls a grandfather “father,” and Joseph’s statement about the religion of his fathers does likewise; a father blocks siblings.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r6.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة على قوله بأن الجد أب والأب يحجب الأخوات والأخوة

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r7.claim: A report from Ata has Ibn Abbas swear at the Black Stone that a grandfather is a father and rebuke Zayd for counting a son’s son as a son but not a father’s father as a father.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r7.anchor: ما روى عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه قال : من شاء لاعنته عند الحجر الأسود ، إن الجد أب

RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r8.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r8.claim: Shafi‘i rejects the equation: because the verse distinguishes Jacob from Abraham’s sons, a grandfather’s upward relation cannot make him literally a father if a grandson is not literally a son.
RAZI-FULL:v4p69#2/r8.anchor: فإن الله تعالى ما أدخل يعقوب في بنيه لأنه ميزه عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r1.claim: A difference in generational rank cannot explain denying the name “father” if grandfather and father share it literally.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r1.anchor: لو كان الاسم حقيقة فيهما جميعا لم يكن الترتيب في الوجود سببا لنفي اسم الأب عنه

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r2.claim: No jurist, linguist, or exegete says that someone dies leaving one mother and many fathers, as would follow if all grandfathers were literal fathers.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r2.anchor: مات وخلف أما وآباء كثيرين وذلك مما لم يطلقه أحد من الفقهاء وأرباب اللغة

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r3.claim: If grandfathers were fathers, Companions would not dispute their inheritance; a grandmother would plainly be a mother, so Abu Bakr would not need to ask about her share.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r3.anchor: لو كان الجد أبا ولا شك أن الصحابة عارفون باللغة لما كانوا يختلفون في ميراث الجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r4.claim: If a grandfather were literally a father, a grandson would be a son and inherit alongside the son under 4:11, which does not happen.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r4.anchor: فلو كان الجد أبا لكان ابن الابن ابنا لا محالة

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r5.claim: Ubayy’s reading omits “your fathers,” but it is anomalous and does not displace the transmitted reading.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r5.anchor: أنه قرأ أبي : { وإلاه * إبراهيم } بطرح آبائك إلا أن هذا لا يقدح في الغرض

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r6.claim: Kinship words for grandfather and uncle are figurative: the Prophet called Abbas the remainder of his fathers and said to return something to his father; the ability to deny the title confirms non-literal use.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r6.anchor: أطلق لفظ الأب على الجد وعلى العم وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام في العباس : ( هذا بقية آبائي )

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas’s designation of grandfather as father concerns legal status, not the lexical meaning of father.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r7.anchor: فإنما أطلق الاسم عليه نظرا إلى الحكم الشرعي لا إلى الاسم اللغوي

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r8.claim: “One God” is an appositive to “the God of your fathers,” like “forelock, a lying forelock,” or a specification meaning they intend one God.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r8.anchor: إلاها واحدا } فهو بدل { إله * آبائك } كقوله : { بالناصية * ناصية كاذبة }

RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r9.claim: “And we submit to Him” can be a circumstantial clause tied to worshipper or worshipped, a clause coordinated with “we worship,” or an emphatic parenthesis of sincerity and monotheism.
RAZI-FULL:v4p70/r9.anchor: أما قوله : { ونحن له مسلمون } ففيه وجوه . أحدها :

STUDYQURAN:2:133/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r1.claim: The Quran’s argument denies exclusive People of the Book ownership of the patriarchs, presenting them as followers of Abraham’s pure religion, primordial monotheism identified with Islam.
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r1.anchor: the patriarchs named here cannot be claimed by the People of the Book in an exclusive and narrow way

STUDYQURAN:2:133/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r2.claim: Jacob’s story is developed in Sūrah 12 through the account of his son Joseph, and Jacob appears in other prophet lists.
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r2.anchor: The story of Jacob (Abraham’s grandson through Isaac) and his children is more fully discussed in Sūrah 12

STUDYQURAN:2:133/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r3.claim: Here ilāh means the generic noun god, not the proper name Allāh.
STUDYQURAN:2:133/r3.anchor: In this verse the God translates ilāh

TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r1.claim: Am kuntum shahada is a fresh question after prior speech, asking whether the Jews and Christians witnessed Jacob’s death; they did not, so must not falsely claim the patriarchs followed their religions.
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r1.anchor: أكنتم يا معشر اليهود والنصارى المكذبين بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، الجاحدين نبوته، حضور يعقوب

TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r2.claim: The verse refutes Jewish and Christian claims about Abraham and Jacob: God sent them and their descendants upon the upright submission to God, which they taught their children.
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r2.anchor: ابتعثت خليلي إبراهيم وولده إسحاق وإسماعيل وذريتهم بالحنيفية المسلمة

TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v2p585#2/r3.claim: The address asking who witnessed Jacob’s final instruction is directed to the People of the Book.

TAB-FULL:v2p586/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r1.claim: The second idh restates the first in apposition: Jacob spoke to his sons when death approached, asking what they would worship after his death.
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r1.anchor: يعقوب إذ قال يعقوب لبنيه حين حضور موته

TAB-FULL:v2p586/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r2.claim: Jacob’s sons answered that they would worship the one God of Jacob and their forefathers, dedicating worship and lordship to Him alone without associating anything with Him.
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r2.anchor: نخلص له العبادة ونوحد له الربوبية فلا نشرك به شيئا

TAB-FULL:v2p586/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r3.claim: Muslimun may be a circumstantial description of their worship or a separate statement that they remain submissive afterward; al-Tabari prefers the circumstantial reading.
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r3.anchor: وأحسن هذين الوجهين في تأويل ذلك أن يكون بمعنى الحال

TAB-FULL:v2p586/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r4.claim: Ishmael is listed before Isaac because he was older.

TAB-FULL:v2p586/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r5.claim: The anomalous reading أبيك is mistaken: Arabic can call an uncle a father, so Ishmael belongs among the forefathers; the canonical reading آبائك is supported by the readers’ consensus, and ilahan is circumstantial accusative.
TAB-FULL:v2p586/r5.anchor: والصواب من القراءة عندنا في ذلك: {وإله آبائك}

TAB-FULL:v2p597/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r1.claim: Being Muslim means submission through obedience and worship; the prophetic response identifies those who affirm all revelation as Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r1.anchor: لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

TAB-FULL:v2p597/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r2.claim: When Jews asked which messengers he believed in, Muhammad affirmed all revelation, including Jesus; they rejected Jesus, prompting the response in 5:59.
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r2.anchor: فلما ذكر عيسى جحدوا نبوته وقالوا: لا نؤمن بعيسى

TAB-FULL:v2p597/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r3.claim: A second version of the report names Nafiʿ ibn Abi Nafiʿ where the first version named Rafiʿ ibn Abi Rafiʿ.
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r3.anchor: قال: ونافع بن أبي نافع، مكان رافع بن أبي رافع

TAB-FULL:v2p597/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r4.claim: The command to affirm all revelation requires believers to believe in every prophet and messenger without distinguishing among them.
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r4.anchor: أمر الله المؤمنين أن يؤمنوا ويصدقوا بأنبيائه ورسله كلهم

TAB-FULL:v2p597/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r5.claim: The twelve sons of Jacob each became the ancestor of a people, so they were called the tribes.
TAB-FULL:v2p597/r5.anchor: الأسباط: يوسف وإخوته بنو يعقوب، ولد اثني عشر رجلا

TAB-FULL:v2p598/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r1.claim: Al-Suddi lists Jacob’s sons as Joseph, Benjamin, Reuben, Judah, Simeon, Levi, Dan, and Kohath.
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r1.anchor: أما الأسباط فهم بنو يعقوب: يوسف، وبنيامين،

TAB-FULL:v2p598/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Jacob’s twelve sons each fathered a people, forming the tribes.
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r2.anchor: الأسباط: يوسف وإخوته بنو يعقوب اثنا عشر رجلا، فولد لكل رجل

TAB-FULL:v2p598/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives Jacob’s genealogy and wives’ children, concluding that the twelve sons became twelve tribes whose number and lineages only God knows.
TAB-FULL:v2p598/r3.anchor: فكان بنو يعقوب اثني عشر رجلا، نشر الله منه اثني عشر سبطا

TABATABAI:2:133/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133/r1.claim: The cited declaration that religion with God is Islam confirms that Islam is the religion Abraham brought and that his descendants inherited.

TABATABAI:2:133/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133/r2.claim: Calling Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac fathers uses father for an ancestor, uncle, or parent without ellipsis; this supports Abraham’s later address to Azar as father.
TABATABAI:2:133/r2.anchor: إطلاق لفظ الأب على الجد والعم والوالد من غير مصحح للتغليب

TABATABAI:2:133/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133/r3.claim: The concise phrase “one God” after naming Jacob’s and his fathers’ God prevents the mistaken inference that they worship different gods, as polytheists do.
TABATABAI:2:133/r3.anchor: في هذا الإيجاز بعد الإطناب بقوله

TABATABAI:2:133/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133/r4.claim: Their submission explains that worship must follow Islam; Islam alone is Abraham’s religion inherited by Isaac, Jacob, Ishmael, Israelites, and Abraham’s descendants, leaving no warrant to replace it.
TABATABAI:2:133/r4.anchor: بيان للعبادة وأنها ليست عبادة كيفما اتفقت بل عبادة على نهج الإسلام

TABATABAI:2:133/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:133/r5.claim: Samaʿa reports al-Sadiq’s analogy: faith relates to Islam as the Kaaba to the sacred precinct; one can be in the precinct without being in the Kaaba, but not vice versa.
TABATABAI:2:133/r5.anchor: عن سماعة عن الصادق عليه السلام الإيمان من الإسلام بمنزلة الكعبة الحرام من الحرم

TABATABAI:2:133/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r6.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:133/r6.claim: Samaʿa reports al-Sadiq defining Islam as professing God’s oneness and affirming the Messenger, which protects life and governs marriage, inheritance, and public status; faith is inward guidance and confirmation.
TABATABAI:2:133/r6.anchor: عن سماعة أيضا عن الصادق عليه السلام قال الإسلام شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله والتصديق برسول الله

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.claim: The preceding reports describe the first level of Islam and faith.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.anchor: وهي تدل على ما مر بيانه من المرتبة الأولى من الإسلام والإيمان

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r2.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r2.claim: Al-Burqi transmits from Ali that Islam means surrender and surrender is certainty; the author places this and the next report at the third level of faith and Islam.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r2.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام قال الإسلام هو التسليم، والتسليم هو اليقين

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r3.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r3.claim: Al-Sadiq says even people who worship, pray, give alms, fast, and pilgrimage become polytheists if they inwardly object to God’s or His Messenger’s acts; the author classifies this as the third level.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r3.anchor: ثم قالوا لشيء صنعه الله أو صنعه رسول الله

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r4.speaker: الله
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r4.claim: In a Miʿraj report to Ahmad, God calls the happiest life constant remembrance, gratitude, awareness of divine rights, and seeking God’s pleasure day and night.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r4.anchor: قال الله سبحانه يا أحمد هل تدري أي عيش أهنىء وأي حيوة أبقى

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r5.speaker: الله
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r5.claim: The same report describes lasting life as preferring God’s will, diminishing worldly attractions, guarding the heart from Satan, and becoming inwardly illuminated by divine love.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r5.anchor: وأما الحياة الباقية فهي التى يعمل لنفسه حتى تهون عليه الدنيا،

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r6.speaker: الله
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r6.claim: Those who act for God’s pleasure receive gratitude, remembrance, and love free of their opposites; God then discloses hidden knowledge and eases death, the grave, and judgment.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r6.anchor: فمن عمل برضاي ألزمه ثلاث خصال أعرفه شكرا لا يخالطه الجهل

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r7.claim: The Miʿraj report concerns the fourth level of Islam and faith.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r7.anchor: وهذا مقام الراضين فمن عمل برضاي ألزمه ثلاث خصال

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r1.speaker: حارثة بن مالك
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r1.claim: Asked by the Prophet about true faith, Haritha says he has renounced worldly life, stays awake and thirsty, and seems to witness the Throne, Paradise, and Hell; the Prophet says God illuminated his heart and urges him to remain firm.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r1.anchor: يا حارثة بن مالك النعماني؟ فقال يا رسول الله مؤمن حقا

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r2.claim: The Haritha report concerns the fourth level of Islam and faith; reports about each level’s details will follow elsewhere, and Qur’anic verses support them.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r2.anchor: والروايتان تحومان حوم المرتبة الرابعة من الإسلام والإيمان

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r3.claim: Each level of Islam and faith has a corresponding form of unbelief or association; the subtler and higher the level, the harder it is to escape its counterpart.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r3.anchor: لكل مرتبة من مراتب الإسلام والإيمان معنى من الكفر والشرك يقابله

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r4.claim: A lower level of Islam or faith does not prevent the presence and effects of higher-level unbelief or association; this explains Qur’anic inner readings beyond a verse’s outward application.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r4.anchor: كل مرتبة من مراتب الإسلام والإيمان الدانية، لا ينافي الكفر

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r5.speaker: الإمام عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r5.claim: A report on “We have more” interprets the added reward as beholding God’s mercy.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r5.anchor: قال عليه السلام النظر إلى رحمة الله

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r6.claim: The Prophet reports God’s promise to the righteous of what no eye has seen, no ear heard, and no human heart imagined; the author says these reports follow from his account of righteousness.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r6.anchor: أعددت لعبادي الصالحين ما لا عين رأت، ولا أذن سمعت

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r7.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r7.claim: Al-Baqir says Jacob’s question about his sons’ worship at death applies to the Qaʾim.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r7.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام أنها جرت في القائم

TABATABAI:2:133#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r8.speaker: الصافي
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r8.claim: Al-Safi proposes that the application is to the Qaʾim from Muhammad’s family: each of them asks his sons this question at death and receives the same answer.
TABATABAI:2:133#2/r8.anchor: قال في الصافي لعل مراده أنها في قائم آل محمد فكل قائم منهم يقول ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r1.claim: أم means بل (‘rather’): the sense is ‘Rather, were you witnesses when Jacob was near death?’; the second إذ is an emphatic apposition in the accusative like the first.
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r1.anchor:
المعنى: بل أكنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت، إذ قال لبنيه "
فقولك: (إذ) الثانية، موضعها نصب كموضع الأولى، وهذا بدل مؤكد.

ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r2.claim: Some read ‘the god of your father’ in the singular to avoid calling the uncle a father; Abraham then clarifies father, while Ishmael and Isaac are also genitive as additional gods.
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r2.anchor:
وقال بعضهم: (وإله أبيك) كأنه كره أن يجعل
العم أباه، وجعل إبراهيم بدلا من أبيك

ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r3.claim: The agreed plural reading آبائك makes Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac genitive appositions explaining ‘your fathers.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p212/r3.anchor: ومن قال: (وإله آبائك) فجمع وهو المجتمع عليه، جعل إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق بدلا،

TABATABAI:6:74-83#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#8/r2.claim: Arabic permits ab for a grandfather, uncle, stepfather, guardian, or respected elder; the Qur’an likewise calls Abraham and Ishmael the fathers of Jacob and Isaac the father of Joseph.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#8/r2.anchor: واللغة تسوغ إطلاق الأب على الجد والعم وزوج أم الإنسان بعد أبيه وكل من يتولى أمور الشخص وكل كبير مطاع

TABRISI:2:133/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r1.claim: Witnesses are those present; the root denotes presence as opposed to absence and yields related words for gatherings, racing, and a person's courtyard.

TABRISI:2:133/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r2.claim: أم is discontinuous, meaning بل plus a question, while the sense is denial: the addressees were not witnesses; the interrogative form makes the proof more forceful.
TABRISI:2:133/r2.anchor: أم ها هنا منقطعة وهي لا تجيء إلا وقد تقدمها كلام لأنها التي تكون بمعنى بل

TABRISI:2:133/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r3.claim: The first إذا is governed by شهداء, while the second may be governed by حضر; either parsing is valid.
TABRISI:2:133/r3.anchor: وإذ الأولى ظرف من قوله شهداء وإذ الثانية بدل من إذ الأولى

TABRISI:2:133/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r4.claim: إلها واحدا may be a circumstantial phrase or apposition to إلهك; ونحن له مسلمون may likewise be circumstantial or a fresh sentence.
TABRISI:2:133/r4.anchor: منصوب على أحد وجهين أن يكون حالا

TABRISI:2:133/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r5.claim: The patriarch names are genitive appositions to آبائك.
TABRISI:2:133/r5.anchor: في موضع جر على البدل من آبائك كما تقول مررت بالقوم

TABRISI:2:133/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r6.claim: Addressing the People of the Book, God denies they witnessed Jacob's deathbed and rejects claims that the prophets were Jews or Christians; Jacob commended pure monotheism, not Judaism.
TABRISI:2:133/r6.anchor: فلا تدعوا على أنبيائي ورسلي الأباطيل بأن تنسبوهم إلى اليهودية والنصرانية

TABRISI:2:133/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r7.claim: The question asks what they will worship, rather than whom, because people then worshipped idols.
TABRISI:2:133/r7.anchor: لأن الناس كانوا يعبدون الأصنام فقال أي الأشياء تعبدون من بعدي

TABRISI:2:133/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133/r8.claim: Ishmael is named before Isaac because he was older; although Jacob's uncle, Ishmael is called his father as Arabs also call an uncle a father, due the honor owed him.
TABRISI:2:133/r8.anchor: وإنما قدم ذكر إسماعيل على إسحاق لأنه كان أكبر منه

TABRISI:2:133/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133/r9.speaker: author
