TABRISI:2:133/r9.claim: The author says Arabic calls Jacob’s uncle Ishmael a father because uncles and grandfathers receive a father’s honor, then introduces a Prophetic report supporting the usage.
TABRISI:2:133/r9.anchor: وإسماعيل كان عم يعقوب وجعله أبا له لأن العرب تسمي العم أبا كما تسمي الجد أبا

TABRISI:2:133#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133#2/r1.claim: They were submissive, acknowledging servitude; another explanation emphasizes humility and surrender in belief and practice.
TABRISI:2:133#2/r1.anchor: أي مذعنون مقرون بالعبودية وقيل خاضعون منقادون مستسلمون لأمره ونهيه

TABRISI:2:133#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:133#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:133#2/r2.claim: A further interpretation takes مسلمون to mean that they entered Islam, supported by the verse saying God's religion is Islam.
TABRISI:2:133#2/r2.anchor: وقيل داخلون في الإسلام يدل عليه قوله

THALABI:v1p280/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p280/r6.claim: The question about witnessing Jacob's death was revealed concerning Jews who claimed that Jacob had bequeathed Judaism to his sons.
THALABI:v1p280/r6.anchor: الآية نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا للنبي

THALABI:v1p280/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v1p280/r7.claim: When Jacob entered Egypt and saw people worshiping idols and fire, he gathered his sons out of concern they would do likewise.
THALABI:v1p280/r7.anchor: الكلبي: لما دخل يعقوب مصر رآهم يعبدون الأوثان والنيران فجمع ولده

THALABI:v1p280/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r8.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v1p280/r8.claim: God gives each prophet a choice between life and death; Jacob asked to delay death so he could consult and advise his children, then gathered sons and grandchildren.
THALABI:v1p280/r8.anchor: عطاء: إن الله لم يقبض نبيا حتى يخيره بين الموت والحياة

THALABI:v1p280/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p280/r9.claim: Jacob asks what his sons will worship after him, and they answer that they worship the one God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.
THALABI:v1p280/r9.anchor: قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم الآية

THALABI:v1p280/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r10.speaker: أبي
THALABI:v1p280/r10.claim: He reads the phrase as your God and the God of Abraham and Ishmael.
THALABI:v1p280/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي: إلهك وإله إبراهيم وإسماعيل

THALABI:v1p280/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r11.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر الجحدري
THALABI:v1p280/r11.claim: He reads the singular your father, since Ishmael was Jacob's uncle, not his father.
THALABI:v1p280/r11.anchor: يحيى بن يعمر الجحدري: وإله أبيك على الواحد، قالوا: لأن إسماعيل عم يعقوب

THALABI:v1p280/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p280/r12.claim: The common reading has fathers in the plural because Arabs call a paternal uncle a father and describe him as his father's counterpart.
THALABI:v1p280/r12.anchor: وقرأ العامة: آبائك على الجمع وقالوا: عم الرجل صنو أبيه

THALABI:v1p282/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p282/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p282/r1.claim: A prophetic expression calls an uncle part of one's forefathers: this is what remains of my fathers.
THALABI:v1p282/r1.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «هذا بقية آبائي»

THALABI:v1p282/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p282/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p282/r2.claim: Another prophetic expression asks that his father be brought lest Quraysh treat him as they treated ʿUrwa ibn Masʿud; this means al-ʿAbbas.
THALABI:v1p282/r2.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «هذا بقية آبائي» ، وقال أيضا: «ردوا علي أبي فإني أخشى أن يفعل به قريش

THALABI:v1p282/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p282/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p282/r3.claim: Arabs call an uncle father and a maternal aunt mother; the verse about Joseph's parents on the throne refers to Jacob and Joseph's maternal aunt.
THALABI:v1p282/r3.anchor: والعرب تسمي العم أبا وتسمي الخالة أما قال الله تعالى ورفع أبويه

THALABI:v1p282/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p282/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p282/r4.claim: Ilahan wahidan means that they acknowledge and worship Him as the one God.
THALABI:v1p282/r4.anchor: إلها واحدا أي نعرفه ونعبده إلها واحدا

ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r1.claim: The address concerns the religious traditions the Israelites follow; here am means “rather” or “nay, but,” not an interrogative, because it is syntactically unconnected to the preceding sentence.
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r1.anchor: sometimes - and especially when it is syntactically unconnected with the preceding sentence, as in this case

ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r2.claim: In this construction am is equivalent to bal and carries no question.
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n107/r2.anchor: it is an equivalent of bal ("rather", or "nay, but"), and has no interrogative connotation

ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r1.claim: In classical Arabic and ancient Hebrew, “father” could mean a grandfather, distant ancestor, or paternal uncle, explaining Ishmael’s inclusion as Jacob’s uncle.
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r1.anchor: the term ab ("father") was applied not only to the direct male parent but also to grandfathers

ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r2.claim: Ishmael is named before Isaac because he was Abraham’s firstborn son.
ASAD-NOTES:2:133#n108/r2.anchor: Since he was the first-born of Abraham's sons, his name precedes that of Isaac

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r1.claim: The passage was revealed concerning Jews who claimed Jacob had enjoined Judaism on his sons at his death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r1.anchor: نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا للنبي صلى الله وسلم: ألست تعلم أن يعقوب يوم مات أوصى بنيه باليهودية؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq reads am as bal: the discourse turns from the previous point and asks whether they were witnesses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r2.anchor: ومعناه: بل أكنتم، كأنه ترك الكلام الأول واستفهم، قاله أبو إسحاق (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes am to mean hal, citing al-Akhṭal’s question about whether one saw Wāsiṭ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r3.anchor: قاله أبو إسحاق (¬2). وقال أبو عبيدة:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r4.claim: Alternatively an initial question is understood: did the Jews learn what they attribute to Jacob, or were they present at his testament? The use of am was explained at 2:108.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يتقدمه استفهام مضمر، كأنه قيل لليهود: أبلغكم ما تقولون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r5.claim: Shuhadāʾ means those present; idh is accusative as a time expression; the source also defines ḥuḍūr as opposite absence and ḥaḍrat as a man’s courtyard.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p344/r5.anchor: الحضور خلاف الغيبة، وحضرة الرجل: فناؤه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r1.claim: The second idh is accusative like the first and is an emphatic substitute for it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r1.anchor: إذ هذه الثانية موضعها نصب، كموضع الأولى، وهو بدل مؤكد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r2.claim: Ab has dialect forms abuka, abak, and abuk, with different duals and plurals; the source cites Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā and Sibawayh as poetic evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r2.anchor: وفي الأب لغات، يقال: هذا أبك، وهذا أباك، وهذا أبوك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r3.claim: Al-Layth says yaʾbū Tayman means to nourish him and taʾabbā so-and-so means to adopt him as a father; diminutives of abāʾ include abiyūn and abiyāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p346/r3.anchor: الليث: فلان يأبو تيما إباوة بكسر الألف، أي: يغذوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r1.claim: Ishmael is grouped with Jacob’s fathers although he was his uncle, because Arabs call an uncle a father.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r1.anchor: أدخله في جملة الأباء، وهو كان عم يعقوب؛ لأن العرب تسمي العم أبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r2.claim: A report about the conquest of Mecca has the Prophet call his uncle al-ʿAbbās his father and say an uncle is a counterpart of his father, confirming Arabic usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r2.anchor: يا عم، أما علمت أن عم الرجل صنو أبيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r3.claim: A reading has wa-ilāhi abīka Ibrāhīm; it may use plural abīn, or singular abīka may exclude Ishmael from the fathers and imply God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r3.anchor: أحدهما: أنه جمع الأب على أبين كما ذكرنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r4.claim: A report says every prophet was offered a choice between life and death; Jacob delayed his death to consult his twelve sons and their descendants, then asked whom they would worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p347/r4.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: إن الله لم يقبض نبيا حتى يخيره بين الموت والحياة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p349/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p349/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p349/r1.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan can be circumstantial, worshipping God in a state of unity, or apposition, whose benefit is to state monotheism explicitly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p349/r1.anchor: ينتصب على وجهين: إن شئت على الحال، كأنهم قالوا: نعبد إلهك في حال وحدانية،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r1.claim: The discourse turns back to the Jews: “Were you witnesses?” means “Rather, were you present?” when Jacob was dying.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r1.anchor: ترك الكلام الأول، وعاد إلى مخاطبة اليهود

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r2.claim: The Jews claimed Jacob advised his sons to follow Judaism; God refutes them because they were not present at his deathbed testament asking whom they would worship after him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:133-135/r2.anchor: فأكذبهم الله تعالى، وقال: أكنتم حاضرين وصيته

ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r1.claim: Jacob's deathbed question asks his sons what they will worship after him, and they affirm worship of one God and submission to Him.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r1.anchor: Benden sonra neye ibadet ve kulluk edeceksiniz?

ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r2.claim: Jacob asked at his last breath to renew his earlier charge, modeling the duty to die as a Muslim for his children.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r2.anchor: son nefesinde bu suâli sormuş ve hakikaten İsrâil, Abdullah olduğunu ve İslâm üzere ölmek vasiyetinin numûnesini evlâdına göstermiş idi

ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r3.claim: By naming Abraham and Ishmael among their forefathers, Jacob's sons show their Abrahamic kinship and that they are descendants of Abraham as well as Israel.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r3.anchor: Ya‘kūb’un dedesi İbrâhim’den ve amcası İsmâil’den başladılar

ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r4.claim: The Torah's promised prophet like Moses from Israel's brothers is from Ishmael's descendants; Jacob's sons called Ishmael their father, while no such prophet came from Israel.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r4.anchor: Benî İsrâil’den böyle bir peygamber gelmemiştir. Ve bu sizden değil ihvânınızdan gelecektir

ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r5.claim: The Torah passage attributed to Moses foretells a prophet like him arising from among Israel's brothers, which Elmalılı identifies with the Ishmaelites.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#4/r5.anchor: İlâhınız Rab teâlâ size aranızdan ve ihvânınızdan bana benzer bir nebî

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r1.claim: Elmalılı reads Habakkuk's description of the Lord appearing from Sinai and holy Paran as a prophecy of Muhammad and his Companions, especially at Mecca's conquest.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r1.anchor: Allah Tûr-i Sînâ’dan, kudsî Cebel-i Fârân’dan geldi

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r2.claim: Christian copies are also reported to read the final phrase as Muhammad appearing for his community's salvation and to redeem the Messiah.

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r3.claim: Elmalılı reads Isaiah's description of the distant-born visitors, pilgrimage, and Quraysh's sanctuary as referring to Mecca and its later prominence.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r3.anchor: Çünkü sen Ümmü’l-kurâ’sın. İmdi sâir bilâd evlâdı keenne Mekke’nin evlâdı

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r4.claim: He identifies the promised new praise with the Muslim talbiya after Mecca's conquest and contrasts it with the pagan formula that included a partner.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r4.anchor: ihdas olunan hamd de لَبَّيْكَ اَللّٰهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r5.speaker: Seman
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r5.claim: Seman's Torah commentary reports God's promise to bless Ishmael, give him twelve princes, and make him the leader of a great nation; Elmalılı identifies that nation with Muhammad's community.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r5.anchor: Tevrat müfessirlerinden Seman Tevrat’ın sifr-i evvelinde şunu rivayet etmiştir

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r6.claim: A Greek Torah translation says Jacob told his sons that prophecy would continue among them until the coming messenger, after whom their prophecy and sovereignty would cease.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r6.anchor: Gelecek resul gelmediği müddetçe bizden nübüvvet munkatı‘olmaz, o geldikten sonra bizden nübüvvet ve saltanat munkatı‘olur

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r7.claim: A Greek Psalm text predicts a future lawgiving prophet whose light reaches east and west, whose first followers are Arabs, and whose enduring law is obeyed by rulers.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r7.anchor: Yani Hak teâlâ vahiy tarîkiyle Dâvûd’a buyurdu ki

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r8.claim: A Gospel saying attributed to Jesus describes a later figure who existed before Jesus and whose sandal strap Jesus is unworthy to untie.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r8.anchor: benden evvel halk olunmuştur. Ben onun papucu bağını çözmek

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r9.claim: Jesus's Paraclete saying describes a messenger who speaks only what is revealed; Elmalılı links this to Quranic statements that Muhammad follows revelation rather than personal desire.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r9.anchor: Ben gideceğim ve size Faraklit Rûhu’l-hak gelecektir ki kendi tarafından tekellüm etmez

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r10.claim: One interpretation takes Faraklit to mean an intercessor who is interceded for, a quality of the Messenger.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r10.anchor: Birisi, şâfi‘müşeffa‘demektir ki Resûlullah’ın bir sıfatıdır

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r11.speaker: Nasârâ
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r11.claim: Some Christians explain Faraklit as the separator of truth and falsehood, deriving it from Faruk with a Greek intensifying suffix; Elmalılı says this also names the Prophet as possessor of the criterion.

ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r12.claim: Elmalılı condemns the Christians' refusal to understand these scriptural signs as sheer error.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#5/r12.anchor: Ve Nasârânın bu âyetleri anlamak istememeleri

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r1.claim: Elmalılı argues that the old scriptures preserve prophecies of Muhammad whose meanings Jews and Christians hide or distort, and that the Quran confirms them; their combined force removes doubt for fair readers.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r1.anchor: bunlar hakkıyla okuyanlar ve cüz’î fehm ve insâfı olanlar için bilhassa hey’et-i mecmû‘asıyla her türlü şüpheyi kesmeye kâfî beyyinâttır

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r2.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Torah promised an unlettered prophet from Ishmael; those who follow and affirm his light receive forgiveness, Paradise, and two rewards for following Moses and Muhammad.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r2.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden rivayet olunduğu üzere Cenâb-ı Allah Tevrat’ta Benî İsrâil’e şöyle bir ahd

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r3.claim: Another transmitted Torah description gives the final Prophet's birthplace as Mecca, home as Tayba, realm as Syria, and community as Hammādūn.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r3.anchor: “mevlidi Mekke’de, meskeni Taybe’de, mülkü Şâm’da ve ümmeti Hammâdûn” diye

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r4.claim: The earlier communities were promised a future culminating Prophet and were required to believe in him before his arrival, accepting God's covenant in each revealed book.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r4.anchor: Bâlâda nakledilen ve elyevm mevcud bulunan kütüb-i sâlife âyetleri de kat‘iyyen gösteriyor ki Cenâb-ı Allah öteden beri

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r5.claim: Mosaic religion is not the beginning and Christianity is not the final dispensation: Jesus was not the prophet like Moses, and the Gospel itself announced a later possessor of the criterion and spirit of truth.

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r6.claim: God's first address to the Israelites demands that they fulfil their covenant and believe the revelation confirming what they already possess.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r6.anchor: emirleriyle bu ahdin icrâ-yı îcâbını talep etmiş

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.claim: The Abraham story and Jacob's testament clarify the meaning of Israel's brothers and the value of Islam.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.anchor: kıssa-i İbrâhim’deki kelimâta ve vasiyyet-i Ya‘kūb’a nazar-ı dikkati celb ederek ihvânın mânasını, İslâmın kıymetini tefhim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.claim: Abraham bequeathed the religion to his children and later generations; Jacob repeated the bequest to his sons, charged them to keep monotheism, and received their pledge to continue it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.anchor: Hz. Ya‘kub’un da kendi oğullarına aynı vasiyeti tekrar ettiği, tevhid inancından sapmamalarını emrettiği; onların da tevhid geleneğini yaşatacaklarına dair söz verdikleri bildirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r1.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r1.claim: Most exegetes take the opening em as an interrogative expressing rejection: Jews were not present at Jacob's death, so how can they claim his religion matches theirs when he reaffirmed Abraham's monotheism and took his sons' pledge?
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r1.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğu bu âyetin başındaki “em” kelimesinin soru edatı olduğunu ve red anlamı taşıdığını ifade ederler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r2.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r2.claim: Razi allows em to function as a conjunction: Israelite ancestors witnessed Jacob call his sons to Islam and monotheism, so their descendants know this and should not make improper claims about prophets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:133/r2.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî, “em” edatının bağlaç olarak da alınabileceğini belirtir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Jews who told the Prophet that Jacob had instructed his sons to follow Judaism when he died.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41/r1.anchor: نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ألست تعلم أن يعقوب يوم مات أوصى بنيه باليهودية

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، يحيى بن يعمر، عاصم الجحدري، أبو رجاء
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r1.claim: They read وإله أبيك with the singular form of أب, which Abu al-Fath interprets collectively as referring to Jacob's forefathers.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r1.anchor: قراءة ابن عباس والحسن ويحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري وأبي رجاء

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r2.claim: Abīk can be a sound plural of أب meaning forefathers; the following names appose a plural, so this reading needs no forced singular-for-plural interpretation.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p112/r2.anchor: "أبيك" جمع أب على الصحة، على قولك للجماعة: هولاء أبون أحرار

QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#1/r1.claim: Ibrāhīma is the standard canonical form, with long ī before final mīm.
QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#1/r1.anchor: Standard canonical form: Ibrāhīma with long ī before final mīm

QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#2/r1.claim: Ibrāhāma is a canonical phonological adaptation of the same foreign name, using ā rather than ī before mīm.
QIRAAT-ER:2:133:22#2/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with fatḥa + alif (ā) instead of kasra + yāʾ (ī) before mīm

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb as the prophet’s name is a foreign proper noun and therefore indeclinable; the Arabic word for a male partridge is declinable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r3.anchor: يعقوب: اسم أعجمي ممنوع الصرف للعلمية والعجمة الشخصية، ويعقوب عربي، وهو ذكر القبج،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r4.claim: The folk explanations that Jacob was named for following his twin or having many descendants fail, since an Arabic derivation would make the name declinable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r4.anchor: ومن زعم أن يعقوب النبي إنما سمي يعقوب لأنه هو وأخوه العيص توأمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r1.claim: Ḥuḍūr means witnessing or being present; the verb’s kasra form unusually uses a ḍamma imperfect, like a small set of anomalous Arabic verbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r1.anchor: الحضور: الشهود، تقول منه: حضر بفتح العين، وفي المضارع: يحضر بضمها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r2.claim: Isḥāq as a name is a foreign proper noun and indeclinable, while the verbal noun from asḥaq would be declinable if used as a name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r2.anchor: إسحاق: اسم أعجمي لا ينصرف للعلمية والعجمة الشخصية، وإسحاق: مصدر أسحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r3.claim: Grammarians offer several broken plurals for Ishaq, Jacob, and Israel; Kufans propose forms such as asāḥiq and yaʿāqiba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r3.anchor: وقالوا في الجمع: أساحقة وأساحيق، وفي جمع يعقوب: يعاقبة ويعاقيب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r4.claim: Abu al-Abbas rejects Kufan plurals that drop the hamza, arguing it is not an augment; he allows forms like abārih and asāmīʿ and recommends sound plurals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p634/r4.anchor: رد أبو العباس على من أسقط الهمزة، لأن هذا ليس موضع زيادتها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r1.claim: In “do not let me see you here,” the speaker does not ban seeing itself but the listener’s presence that would cause it; the phrasing conveys anger and aversion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r1.anchor: لا أرينك هاهنا، لا ينهى نفسه عن الرؤية، ولكن المعنى على النهي عن حضوره في هذا المكان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r7.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Jews who claimed Jacob prescribed Judaism: on reaching Egypt, Jacob saw idol and celestial worship and asked his sons what they would worship after him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي: لما دخل يعقوب مصر رآهم يعبدون الأوثان والنيرين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r8.claim: The revelation informs the Prophet of Jacob’s actual testament and refutes the Jewish claim that he died a Jew.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r8.anchor: فأنزل الله هذه الآية إعلاما لنبيه بما وصى به يعقوب، وتكذيبا لليهود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r1.claim: Most grammarians take disjunctive am as “rather, were you witnesses?”; it shifts topic without canceling the preceding statement and rebukes the audience by implying they were not witnesses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r1.anchor: أنها هنا منقطعة بمعنى بل والهمزة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r2.claim: Another reading takes am as “rather,” saying the audience—or their ancestors whose reports they inherited—were witnesses, thereby challenging the Jewish attribution of Judaism to Jacob.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r2.anchor: وقيل: أم هنا بمعنى: بل، والمعنى بل كنتم، أي كان أسلافكم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads it as a reproachful question: did you witness Jacob’s testament and claim knowledge, when in fact you did not and are inventing the claim?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r3.anchor: قال لهم على جهة التقرير والتوبيخ أشهدتم يعقوب وعلمتم بما أوصى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r4.speaker: بعض النحويين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r4.claim: A Yemeni dialect reportedly permits am to mean the interrogative hamza at the start of a sentence; Abu Hayyan has not found this in grammarians.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r4.anchor: وأم تكون بمعنى ألف الاستفهام في صدر الكلام لغة يمانية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r5.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says am can introduce a question mid-sentence after an earlier clause, as in “or do they say he invented it?”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r5.anchor:
وحكى الطبري أن أم يستفهم بها في وسط
كلام قد تقدم صدره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan summarizes three analyses: the common disjunctive “rather + hamza,” “rather” alone, or interrogative hamza alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r6.anchor: وتلخص أن أم هنا فيها ثلاثة أقوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the address could be to believers, who know the event by revelation, or to Jews claiming prophets died Jews; he prefers a connected alternative asking whether they accuse prophets or witnessed Jacob’s insistence on monotheism.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p638/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الخطاب للمؤمنين بمعنى: ما شاهدتم ذلك، وإنما حصل لكم العلم به من طريق الوحي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari’s connected am because it requires deleting the first alternative clause, a deletion unattested in Arabic and turning one question into an incomplete clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r1.anchor: ولا نعلم أحدا أجاز حذف هذه الجملة، ولا يحفظ ذلك، لا في شعر ولا غيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r2.claim: Arabic can omit a preceding coordinated phrase with wāw or fa when context supplies it, and rarely with aw or ḥattā; this does not establish omission before connected am.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r2.anchor: وإما يحذف المعطوف عليه ويبقى المعطوف مع الواو والفاء، إذا دل على ذلك دليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r3.claim: A poet omits the second alternative after connected am (“was her seeking right-guided or not?”) because a positive question entails its negative opposite; other paired contrasts may likewise be omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r3.anchor:
فما أدري أرشد طلابها
يريد: أم غير رشد، فحذف لدلالة الكلام عليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r4.claim: The first idh makes “when Jacob was present” an adverbial of the witnesses’ presence, not an object; “death came” means its causes approached, since a dying person cannot speak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p639/r4.anchor: إذ حضر العامل في إذ شهداء، وذلك على جهة الظرف، لا على جهة المفعول،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r1.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r1.claim: A cited poet has a speaker tell people to seek an excuse because “I am death,” illustrating death as approaching causes rather than the instant of dying.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r2.claim: The expression that death “comes” is a strange euphemism: death is absent but must arrive; a prayer calls death the best absent thing awaited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r2.anchor: وفي قوله: حضر، كناية غريبة، إنه غائب لا بد أن يقدم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r3.claim: The reading ḥaḍira with kasra is a dialect form; its imperfect with ḍamma is anomalous, and the object is advanced before the subject for emphasis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r3.anchor: وقرىء: حضر بكسر الضاد، وقد ذكرنا أن ذلك لغة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r4.claim: The second idh (“when he said to his sons”) substitutes for the first; grammarians differ whether the first governor is repeated or the same governor applies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r4.anchor:
إذ:
بدل من إذ في قوله: إذ حضر، فالعامل فيه إما شهداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r5.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r5.claim: Al-Qaffal treats the second idh as the time of Jacob’s presence, governed by ḥaḍara, effectively making both adverbials refer to one time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r5.anchor: وزعم القفال أن إذ وقت للحضور، فالعامل فيه حضر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r6.claim: Mā is a complete interrogative noun for what is worshipped, grammatically the direct object of the following verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r6.anchor: ما: استفهام عما لا يعقل، وهو اسم تام منصوب بالفعل بعده.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r7.speaker: قائل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r7.claim: If mā can denote both rational and nonrational beings, Jacob’s question can include humans, angels, celestial bodies, and idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r7.anchor: قول من زعم أن ما مبهمة في كل شيء، يكون هنا يقع على من يعقل وما لا يعقل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r8.speaker: قائل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r8.claim: If mā is restricted to nonrational things, it can ask about the nature of an object, as in “What is Zayd, a jurist or a poet?”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r8.anchor: فقيل: هو سؤال عن صفة المعبود، لأن ما يسأل بها عن الصفات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r9.speaker: قائل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r9.claim: Another explanation is that familiar objects of worship then were inanimate, so the sons understood the question and answered that they worship none of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r9.anchor: وقيل: سأل بما لأن المعبودات المتعارفة في ذلك الوقت كانت جمادات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r10.speaker: قائل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r10.claim: One says Jacob used mā instead of man to test his sons and avoid giving them a hint toward a particular person or faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r10.anchor:
وقيل:
استفهم بما عن المعبود تجربة لهم، ولم يقل من لئلا يطرق لهم الاهتداء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r11.claim: The plain sense asks what they will worship; al-Qaffal instead says Jacob urged them to seek only God’s face and feared worldly distraction rather than idol worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r11.anchor:
وظاهر الكلام أنه استفهم عن الذي يعبدون، أي
العبادة المشروعة؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r12.claim: Jacob’s question shows the prophets’ concern for their children was focused on religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r12.anchor: وفي ذلك دليل على أن شفقة الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام على أولادهم كانت في باب الدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p640/r13.anchor: من بعدي: يريد من بعد موتي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r1.claim: It is reported that Jacob, when prophets were offered a choice, chose death but asked first for time to advise his family and sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r1.anchor: وحكي أن يعقوب عليه السلام حين خير، كما يخير الأنبياء، اختار الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r2.claim: The majority read “your fathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac”; Abraham onward can be apposition or clarification of “your fathers,” with an omitted “I mean” also possible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r2.anchor: قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق: هذه قراءة الجمهور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r3.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r3.claim: Ubayy’s reading omits “your fathers,” giving “and the God of Abraham.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبي: وإله إبراهيم، بإسقاط آبائك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وابن يعمر والجحدري وأبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r4.claim: These readers have the singular “your father”; Abraham then clarifies or stands in apposition to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، والحسن، وابن يعمر، والجحدري، وأبو رجاء: وإله أبيك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r5.claim: Calling Abraham and what follows “your fathers” shows that an uncle can be called a father and that a grandfather is also called a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r5.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن العم يطلق عليه أب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas uses these verses and Jacob’s “fathers” in 12:38 to argue that a grandfather inherits as a father when the father is absent, excluding siblings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r6.anchor: وقد استدل ابن عباس بذلك وبقوله: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r7.speaker: الصديق وجماعة من الصحابة وأبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r7.claim: Abu Bakr, a group of Companions, and Abu Hanifa treat the grandfather as the father in inheritance when no father survives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r7.anchor: وهو مذهب الصديق وجماعة من الصحابة، رضوان الله عليهم أجمعين، وهو قول أبي حنيفة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r8.speaker: زيد بن ثابت ومالك وأبو يوسف والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit, Malik, Abu Yusuf, and al-Shafiʿi treat the grandfather like siblings, guaranteeing him a third if division would reduce his share below that.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r8.anchor: وقال زيد بن ثابت: هو بمنزلة الإخوة، ما لم تنقصه المقاسمة من الثلث،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r9.speaker: علي وابن أبي ليلى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r9.claim: Ali and Ibn Abi Layla treat the grandfather as one sibling, guaranteeing him a sixth if division would reduce his share below that.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r9.anchor: وقال علي: هو بمنزلة أحد الإخوة، ما لم تنقصه المقاسمة من السدس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r10.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r10.claim: Sibawayh records أبين as an inflected plural of father, allowing “your father” to be construed as a plural with its nūn dropped in annexation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p641/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع سقطت منه النون للإضافة، فقد جمع أب على أبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r1.claim: The sons repeat the verb “we worship” instead of merely saying “your god,” explicitly matching their answer to Jacob’s question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r1.anchor: وفي إجابتهم له بإظهار الفعل تأكيد لما أجابوه به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r2.claim: Calling God “your god” and “the god of your fathers” emphasizes that questioner and respondents share one deity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r2.anchor: وإضافة الإله إلى يعقوب فيه دليل على اتحاد معبود السائل والمجيب لفظا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r3.claim: Repeating “and the god” before a genitive pronoun follows the usual rule that a conjunction on such a pronoun repeats its preposition; omitting it with an explicit noun would better signal unity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r3.anchor: وإنما كرر لفظ وإله، لأنه لا يصح العطف على الضمير المجرور إلا بإعادة جاره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r4.claim: Jacob is named first because he asked, Abraham because he is the origin, and Ishmael before Isaac because he was older or honored as the Prophet’s ancestor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r4.anchor: وبدأ أولا بإضافة الإله إلى يعقوب، لأنه هو السائل، وقدم إبراهيم، لأنه الأصل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r5.claim: Only these ancestors are named because they were the best people of their eras; the answer does not enumerate every being people worshipped.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r5.anchor: واقتصر على هؤلاء، لأنهم كانوا خير الناس في أزمانهم، ولم يعم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r6.claim: “One God” can be an apposition or a circumstantial qualifier; either makes explicit that one shared deity is a single individual, not several.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r6.anchor: هذه الحال، أو البدل، هو التنصيص على أن معبودهم واحد فرد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses “one God” as specification, but grammarians disallow specification with an indefinite or ambiguous noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r7.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن ينتصب على الاختصاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r8.claim: “We submit to Him” is best read as a second coordinated part of the answer: worship is recurring action, while the nominal “submitting” expresses their permanent surrender.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r8.anchor: والأول أبلغ، وهو أن تكون الجملة معطوفة على قوله: نعبد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the clause parenthetical and explanatory; Abu Hayyan rejects this because it is not inserted between tightly linked parts of one speaker’s statement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p642/r9.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن تكون جملة اعتراضية مؤكدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r1.claim: A parenthetical clause strengthens a relation between parts that belong together, such as a relative clause and antecedent or a condition and result; “we submit to Him” is not such an insertion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r1.anchor: والذي ذكره النحويون أن جملة الاعتراض هي الجملة التي تفيد تقوية بين جزأي موصول وصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r2.claim: The sons’ statement is complete before “we submit,” and God’s statement follows it, so it cannot be a parenthesis inserted by the same speaker between linked parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r2.anchor: لأن قبلها كلاما مستقلا، وبعدها كلام مستقل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads “we submit to Him” as a nominal clause meaning “we were and will be so,” or possibly as a circumstantial clause; he says the first is more laudatory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r3.anchor:
ابن عطية: ونحن له مسلمون ابتداء وخبر، أي:
كذلك كنا ونحن نكون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r4.claim: There is no need to supply Ibn Atiyya’s omitted “thus we were”; the clause can coordinate directly with “we worship,” which is preferable to ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r4.anchor: ومتى أمكن حمل الكلام على غير إضمار، مع صحة المعنى، كان أولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r5.speaker: المقلدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r5.claim: Traditionalists use the sons’ answer as proof that imitation suffices: Jacob’s sons name the deity worshipped by their ancestors, and Jacob does not object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r5.anchor: تمسك بهذه الآية المقلدة، وقالوا: إن أبناء يعقوب اكتفوا بالتقليد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r6.speaker: التعليمية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r6.claim: The Talimiyya argue that God is known only by instruction from a prophet or imam, since the sons appeal to the deity worshipped by Jacob and earlier fathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r6.anchor:
واستدل بها التعليمية، قالوا:
لا طريق لمعرفة الله تعالى إلا بتعليم الرسول والإمام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r7.claim: The verse only records their confession of worship; it does not establish that their belief arose from imitation or instruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p643/r7.anchor: لأن الآية لم تتضمن إلا الإقرار بعبادة الإله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r1.claim: A report addressed to Banu Hashim and Fatima warns that family lineage cannot substitute for one’s deeds or protect one from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r1.anchor: وروي: يا بني هاشم! لا يأتيني الناس بأعمالهم وتأتوني بأنسابكم!

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says this verse refutes the determinists who deny that a servant acquires or performs acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وفي هذه الآية رد على الجبرية القائلين: لا اكتساب للعبد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r3.speaker: الجبرية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r3.claim: The Jabriyya say people are compelled in their acts, have no choice, and relate to action like a branch moved by an external force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r3.anchor: قول الجبرية، وهو أن العبد مجبور على فعله، وأنه لا اختيار له في ذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r4.speaker: القدرية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r4.claim: The Qadariyya deny compulsion and say people possess power to bring their acts into existence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r4.anchor: قول القدرية، وهو أنهم ليسوا مجبورين على الفعل، بل لهم قدرة على إيجاد الفعل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r5.claim: The Muʿtazila say God creates a person’s capacity before the act, leaving the person able either to perform or omit it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r5.anchor: قول المعتزلة، أن العبد له قدرة يخلقها الله له قبل الفعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r6.speaker: أهل السنة والجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r6.claim: The Sunni position is that God creates capacity and empowerment alongside the act; a person performs good or evil without compulsion, and this grounds reward and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r6.anchor: مذهب أهل السنة والجماعة: أن الله يخلق للعبد تمكينا وقدرة مع الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Hasan says created capacity relates to an act without causing it; God creates both, and the servant’s acquisition is that act’s relation to his capacity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r7.anchor: قول أبي الحسن: أن القدرة صفة متعلقة بالمقدور من غير تأثير في المقدور،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r8.speaker: الباقلاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r8.claim: Al-Baqillani says the act itself is not intrinsically obedience or sin; its quality as such arises through the created capacity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r8.anchor: قول الباقلاني: أن ذات الفعل لم تحصل له صفة، كونه طاعة ومعصية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق الأسفرائيني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini says the eternal and created capacities both relate to the act, so the servant’s act occurs through divine assistance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p644#2/r9.anchor: أن القدرتين، القديمة والحديثة، إذا تعلقتا بمقدور وقع بهما،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r4.claim: Jacob asks what his sons will worship after his death to test whether they accept his testament and reassure him that his call to God will continue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r4.anchor: وحكمة هذا السؤال أنه لما وصاهم بالحنيفية، استفسرهم عما تكن صدورهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r5.claim: The question rebukes Jews and Christians: they did not witness Jacob's deathbed testament, and their claims about the patriarchs lack eyewitness, transmitted, or rational proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r5.anchor: وصدر سؤال يعقوب بتقريع اليهود والنصارى بأنهم ما كانوا شهدوا وصية يعقوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that the verse was revealed in response to Jews who told the Prophet that Jacob had instructed his sons to be Jews; this occasion supports addressing Jews of his time.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r1.anchor: فقد ذكر الواحدي أن الآية نزلت في اليهودي حين قالوا للنبي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r2.claim: For Jewish addressees, disconnected am means 'rather' plus a rebuking question: they were absent from Jacob's deathbed and cannot assert what they claim; it may instead ask whether their ancestors witnessed his Islamic testament.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r2.anchor: إما منقطعة بمعنى بل وهمزة الإنكار ومعنى بل الإضراب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r3.claim: A connected am can contrast the known absence with the impossible claim of witnessing, binding the addressees either way: if absent, they invent the report; if present, they contradict the known account.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r3.anchor: وإما متصلة وفي الكلام حذفوالتقدير أكنتم غائبين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that no one is known to permit deleting the clause before connected am; he says deletion is only attested for am with its coordinate.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r4.anchor: وأعترض أبو حيان على هذا الوجه بأنا لا نعلم أحدا أجاز حذف الجملة المعطوف عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r5.claim: Another view addresses believers: the report of earlier prophets' circumstances without hearing or reading is a prophetic sign and a reason to follow the Messenger; its proponent sets aside the weak revelation occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r5.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب للمؤمنين ومعنى بل الإضراب عن الكلام الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r6.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r6.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says he could not find the stated occasion of revelation, a reservation al-Alusi links to the weakness of the believers-address interpretation's disregard of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r6.anchor: حتى قال الإمام السيوطي : لم أقف عليه والشهداءجمع شهيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r7.claim: Shuhadāʾ can mean witnesses or those present; ḥaḍara is read with a kasra in an unusual dialect or by overlap of two patterns.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r7.anchor: والشهداءجمع شهيد أو شاهد بمعنى حاضر وحضر من باب قعد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r8.claim: 'When he said to his sons' is an apposition of inclusion to 'when death came to Jacob,' since both events are intended and the second supplies detail; attaching the first temporal clause to 'they said' breaks the sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390/r8.anchor: إذ قال لبنيه بدل من ( إذ حضر ) بدل اشتمال وكلاهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.claim: In 'what will you worship after me,' mā is nominative with an omitted resumptive pronoun; treating it as an object loses the question's fitting gradation from asking what a thing is to identifying who it is.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.anchor: ما تعبدون من بعدي أي أي شيء تعبدونه بعد موتي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.claim: Jacob's question is not genuine inquiry but a way to urge continued monotheism and Islam and renew their pledge; he reportedly saw fire worship in Egypt and feared for his sons.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.anchor: وفي السؤال عن حالهم بعد موته دليل على أن الغرض حثهم على ما كانوا عليه حال حياته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.claim: The sons' answer is a new sentence responding to the implied question; attributing the deity to several forefathers stresses their shared belief, and Ishmael is named before Isaac because he was older.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.anchor: إستئناف وقع جوابا لسؤال نشأ عن حكاية السؤال وفي إضافة الإله إلى المتعدد إشارة إلى الإتفاق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.claim: Jacob calls his uncle Ishmael a father either by letting the majority outweigh one exception or because uncles and fathers are joined like brothers; a Prophetic report in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs says an uncle is his father's counterpart.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.anchor: وعده من آباء يعقوب مع أنه عمه تغليا للأكثر على الأقل أو لأنه شبه العم بالأب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.claim: A report cited from Ibn Abī Shayba has the Prophet ask that his family honor al-ʿAbbās, since he is the remainder of his forefathers, illustrating broad use of 'fathers.'
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.anchor: والآية على حد ما أخرجه إبن أبي شيبة وغيره من قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads 'abīkum' in the singular, with Ishmael and Isaac coordinated as an appositional clarification; alternatively it may be a plural with the nūn omitted in annexation, as in cited poetry.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r7.claim: 'One God' is an appositional clarification of 'the god of your fathers,' removing any inference of multiple gods; grammarians differ on whether an indefinite apposition must be described.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r7.anchor: والنكرة تبدل من المعرفة بشرط ان توصف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r8.claim: 'We submit to Him' means yielding and affirming servitude, obeying His commands and prohibitions in word and belief, or entering and remaining in Islam; it may be circumstantial or parenthetical.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r8.anchor: أي مذعنون مقرون بالعبودية وقيل : خاضعون منقادون مستسلمون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers coordinating 'we submit' with 'we worship,' making the sons give two answers to Jacob's question and thus an enhanced response.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p390#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الأبلغ أن تكون معطوفة على

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: Am kuntum shuhadāʾ means were you present as witnesses? The address says they were not there when Jacob approached death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: {أم كنتم شهداء} يعني أكنتم شهداء، يريد ما كنتم شهداء حضورا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: One reported occasion is that Jews told Muhammad that Jacob had enjoined Judaism on his sons; on that reading the address is to the Jews.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: قيل: نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألست تعلم أن يعقوب يوم مات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: When Jacob entered Egypt and saw its people worshipping idols and fire, he gathered his children in fear for them and asked whom they would worship after him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لما دخل يعقوب مصر رآهم يعبدون الأوثان والنيران، فجمع ولده وخاف عليهم ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: God lets each prophet choose between life and death; when Jacob was offered the choice, he asked to consult and instruct his children, so God let him gather his children and grandchildren.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: قال عطاء إن الله تعالى لم يقبض نبيا حتى يخيره بين الحياة والموت فلما خير يعقوب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: Ishmael was the sons' paternal uncle, whom Arabs call a father; the Prophet likewise called a man's uncle his father's counterpart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: وكان إسماعيل عما لهم والعرب تسمي العم أبا كما تسمي الخالة أما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "عم الرجل صنو أبيه"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r6.claim: The text also recalls the Prophet calling his uncle al-ʿAbbas his father and fearing Quraysh might treat him as Thaqif treated ʿUrwa b. Masʿud, whom they killed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p154/r6.anchor: "ردوا علي أبي فإني أخشى أن تفعل به قريش ما فعلت ثقيف بعروة بن مسعود"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p155/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p155/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p155/r1.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan is accusative as an appositive to ilāhaka; alternatively, the sense is that they acknowledge Him as one God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p155/r1.anchor: {إلها واحدا} نصب على البدل من قوله إلهك وقيل نعرفه إلها واحدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r1.claim: Am is a disconnected question of denial: the audience was absent at Jacob's death and cannot attribute Judaism to him; alternatively it connects to an omitted question asking whether they were absent or present.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r1.anchor: أم منقطعة ومعنى الهمزة فيها الإنكار، أي ما كنتم حاضرين إذ حضر يعقوب الموت وقال لبنيه ما قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r2.claim: Another view addresses believers: they did not witness the event and know it only through revelation; a reading pronounces ḥaḍara with kasra.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r2.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب للمؤمنين والمعنى ما شاهدتم ذلك وإنما علمتموه بالوحي وقرىء { حضر } بالكسر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r3.claim: The second idh is appositive to the first; Jacob asks what they worship to affirm monotheism and take their pledge to remain in it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r3.anchor: { إذ قال لبنيه } بدل من { إذ حضر }. { ما تعبدون من بعدي } أي: شيء تعبدونه، أراد به تقريرهم على التوحيد والإسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r4.claim: Mā asks about any thing until its identity is known, then about rational beings; it can also ask a person's qualities, as in the example about Zayd.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r4.anchor: وما يسأل به عن كل شيء ما لم يعرف، فإذا عرف خص العقلاء بمن إذا سئل عن تعيينه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r5.claim: The sons identify the acknowledged God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac; Ishmael counts as an ancestor by inclusive usage or because an uncle is like a father.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r5.anchor: المتفق على وجوده وألوهيته ووجوب عبادته، وعد إسماعيل من آبائه تغليبا للأب والجد، أو لأنه كالأب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r6.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r6.claim: The Prophet supports calling an uncle an ancestor by saying a man's uncle is like his father's twin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r6.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام: " عم الرجل صنو أبيه "

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r7.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r7.claim: The Prophet also called al-Abbas the remnant of his forefathers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r7.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام في العباس رضي الله عنه " هذا بقية آبائي "

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r8.claim: A reading has ilāha abīka; it is parsed either as a plural form supported by a poem or as singular with Abraham alone in apposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133/r8.anchor: وقرىء «إله أبيك»، على أنه جمع بالواو والنون كما قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.claim: Ilāhan wāḥidan apposes the God of the forefathers, as in the cited Quranic construction, explicitly states unity, removes a possible misunderstanding from the repeated genitive, and reinforces the claim; it may instead be an accusative specification.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r1.anchor: بدل من إله آبائك كقوله تعالى: بالناصية ناصية كذبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r2.claim: Wa-naḥnu lahu muslimūn may be a circumstantial clause of the subject, object, or both in naʿbudu, or a parenthesis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:133#2/r2.anchor: حال من فاعل نعبد، أو مفعوله، أو منهما، ويحتمل أن يكون اعتراضا.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.claim: The following verses refute the People of Scripture's claims to Judaism or Christianity by demonstrating that Abraham and the prophets were not adherents of those later religions, a falsehood they knew to be false.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.anchor: وبرأ خليله والأنبياء من ذلك على وجه أوجب القطع بأنهم عالمون ببطلانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r1.claim: The opening أم has an omitted alternative: the rebuke may ask whether they were absent or present at Jacob's testament, or whether they lacked knowledge when claiming exclusive Paradise; either way, their scripture already commands the same lesson.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r1.anchor: أكنتم غائبين عن هذه الوصية من إبراهيم ويعقوب عليهما السلام أم حاضرين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r2.claim: The passage warns against following ancestors merely because they are ancestors: one must obey the first Benefactor, God, even when his commands differ from ancestral practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251/r2.anchor: عدم وجوب التقيد بالآباء , وإرشاد إلى توسيع الفكر إلى المنعم الأول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.claim: Asking whether the People of Scripture witnessed Jacob's testament challenges their claim to Paradise: were they present and obedient to his charge, or absent and without grounds for claiming it? Their scripture itself suffices to refute them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r1.anchor: أكنتم شهداء لذلك منه حتى تكونوا ممن ائتمر بأمره في وصيته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.claim: The question whether they were witnesses also means they have no reason to inquire into ancestors: neither lineage nor ancestral deeds benefit them, since a person has only what they themselves earn.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r2.anchor: لأنه ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.claim: Not following Abraham and Jacob in Islam severs religious kinship, which is stronger than blood kinship; the better reading is that Paradise belongs to those who submit with excellence, not exclusively to the People of Scripture.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r3.anchor: لأن نسب الدين أعظم من نسب الماء والطين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.claim: The words ما تعبدون deliberately use ما to cover rational and non-rational objects, forcing the sons' reply to exclude worship of anything unintelligent; من would not secure that effect.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r4.anchor: ولو عبر بمن لم يفد جوابهم هذا التصريح ينفي عبادة شيء مما لا يعقل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.claim: Jacob specifies من بعدي because a successor may act badly after a reformer's death, and because the sons' lifespans do not encompass all later time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r5.anchor: لأن الخليفة كثيرا ما يخلف الغائب بسوء وإن كان مصلحا في حضوره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.claim: Jacob's sons name Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac as the one God worshiped by their father and forefathers; Ishmael is their uncle, a parallel of their father and thus figuratively a father too.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r6.anchor: وإسماعيل } لأنه عم والعم صنو الأب فهو أب مجازا { وإسحاق }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.claim: By saying one God and then that they submit to Him alone, the sons reject associationism and show that worship is directed to God rather than to ancestors; submission means having no choice against his command.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p251#2/r7.anchor: تحقيقا للبراءة من الشرك وتسجيلا على أهل الكتاب بتحتم بطلان قولهم

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r5.claim: The address 'Were you witnesses?' refers to the people of Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {أم كنتم شهداء} يعني أهل مكة

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r6.claim: Jews, Christians, and others did not witness Jacob's deathbed covenant to his sons to worship God alone; they acknowledged it and were witnesses to their submission.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r6.anchor:
عن الحسن في قوله {أم كنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت} الآية
قال: يقول لم تشهد اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says a grandfather is a father, citing the sons' reference to their forefathers.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r7.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أنه كان يقول: الجد أب ويتلو {قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r8.claim: Ishmael is named before Isaac because he was older.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r8.anchor: عن أبي زيد في الآية قال: يقال بدأ باسماعيل لأنه أكبر

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r9.claim: The verse calls an uncle a father.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r9.anchor: عن أبي العالية في الآية قال: سمى العم أبا

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r10.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says both a maternal uncle and paternal uncle can be called a father.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r10.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب قال: الخال والد العم والد

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r11.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r11.claim: Al-Hasan recited the phrase in the singular as 'your father,' treating the forefather as one.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r11.anchor: عن الحسن أنه كان يقرأ (نعبد إلهك وإله أبيك) على معنى الواحد

RAZI-FULL:v18p167#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p167#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p167#2/r6.claim: The aunt can be called a parent either because she fills the mother’s role or because a maternal aunt is like a mother, just as an uncle is like a father.
RAZI-FULL:v18p167#2/r6.anchor: لأن الخالة أم كما أن العم أب ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { وإلاه آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق

JISHUMI:v1p600/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r2.claim: The apparent reading has آبائك in the plural.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r2.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة آبائك على الجمع، وعن يحيى بن يعمر أبيك على الواحد،

JISHUMI:v1p600/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r3.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
JISHUMI:v1p600/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar is reported to read أبيك in the singular, arguing that Ismāʿīl was Yaʿqūb's uncle, not his father; the author rejects this because consensus opposes it.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r3.anchor: قال: إن إسماعيل عم يعقوب لا أبوه، وهذا لا يجوز القراءة به؛ لأن الإجماع على خلافه،

JISHUMI:v1p600/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v1p600/r4.claim: Arabs may call an uncle a father; the Prophet told al-ʿAbbās, “This is the remnant of my fathers.”
JISHUMI:v1p600/r4.anchor: والعرب تسمي العم أبا، وقد قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - للعباس: هذا بقية آبائي.

JISHUMI:v1p600/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r5.claim: Shāhid and ḥāḍir are near-synonyms; the opposite of present is absent.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r5.anchor: الشاهد والحاضر من النظائر، ونقيض الحاضر الغائب، حضر حضورا.

JISHUMI:v1p600/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r6.claim: Abāʾ is the plural of ab; father is literal for a parent and metaphorical for an uncle, by extension and resemblance, so it can be denied of an uncle.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r6.anchor: والآباء واحده الأب، وهو حقيقة في الوالد مجاز في العم به يسمى العم توسعا وتشبيها؛ ولذلك يصح نفيه عنه.

JISHUMI:v1p600/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r7.claim: Am is disconnected, functioning like bal plus an interrogative hamza; it follows prior speech and introduces the challenge whether they witnessed Yaʿqūb's death.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r7.anchor: أم ههنا منقطعة، كقوله تعالى: (الم (1) تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين (2) أم يقولون افتراه بل هو الحق من ربك

JISHUMI:v1p600/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r8.claim: Although phrased as a question, the statement means they were not witnesses; question form strengthens the argument by inviting them to admit the point.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r8.anchor: ويكون معناه الجحد، أي ما كنتم شهداء. ويقال: لم جعل اللفظ على الاستفهام، والمعنى على خلافه؟

JISHUMI:v1p600/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r9.claim: The second إذ may be an appositive to the first, governed by the sense of “witnesses.”
JISHUMI:v1p600/r9.anchor: هي بدل من (إذ) الأولى، والعامل فيها معنى الشاهد،

JISHUMI:v1p600/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r10.claim: Alternatively, the second إذ is governed by the sense of “came upon” in حضر.

JISHUMI:v1p600/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r11.claim: One parsing makes إلها واحدا a circumstantial accusative attached to إلهك.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r11.anchor: فيه قولان: الأول: أنه حال من قوله إلهك،

JISHUMI:v1p600/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p600/r12.claim: Alternatively, it is an appositive to إلهك, with the added benefit of explicitly stating God's unity.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r12.anchor: والثاني: البدل من إلهك، وتكون الفائدة فيه ذكر التوحيد.

JISHUMI:v1p600/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r13.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v1p600/r13.claim: The cited line “Your eye deceived you, or did you see at Wāsiṭ…” illustrates disconnected أم.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r13.anchor: وقال الشاعر: كذبتك عينك أم رأيت بواسط ... غلس الظلام من الرباب خيالا

ITQAN:v3p234/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p234/r3.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p234/r3.claim: The sons of Jacob similarly mention their forefathers in the order of the religion they followed.

DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r2.claim: Ab can mean an uncle; Ismāʿīl was Jacob’s uncle.
DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : الأب بمعنى العم . فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r10.claim: Shahīd can mean someone present, as opposed to absent.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r10.anchor: والسادس : الحاضر . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r5.claim: A third sense is uncle: Ishmael is Jacob’s uncle in the cited verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r5.anchor: والثالث : العم . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r5.claim: Mā can be an interrogative particle.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r5.anchor: والسادس : بمعنى الاستفهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

JISHUMI:v1p601/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r1.claim: One phrase is parsed circumstantially; an alternative gives it no syntactic position because it begins a new sentence.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r1.anchor: قلنا: نصب على الحال، وقيل: لا موضع لها؛ لأنها على الاستئناف

JISHUMI:v1p601/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl are genitive, governed by the same word as آبائك, with Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq coordinated to Ibrāhīm in the apparent reading; the singular reading coordinates without an appositional rendering.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r2.anchor: محله خفض، والعامل فيه ما عمل في آبائك؛ لأنه بدل منه، فأما إسماعيل وإسحاق فعلى القراءة الظاهرة عطف على إبراهيم

JISHUMI:v1p601/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r3.claim: The verse answers the People of the Book: they were not present at Jacob’s death and must not falsely claim that the prophets were Jews or Christians.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r3.anchor: أم كنتم شهداء أي ما كنتم حضورا، والخطاب لأهل الكتاب، والمراد أنكم لم تحضروا ذلك فلا تدعوا على الأنبياء الأباطيل

JISHUMI:v1p601/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r4.speaker: اليهود
JISHUMI:v1p601/r4.claim: The Jews claimed that Jacob prescribed Judaism to his sons when he died; the verse was revealed in response.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r4.anchor: روي أن اليهود قالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: إن يعقوب يوم مات أوصى بنيه باليهودية

JISHUMI:v1p601/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r5.claim: One account says Jacob entered Egypt, saw its people worshipping idols, gathered his sons, and asked what they would worship after him.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r5.anchor: قيل: لما دخل يعقوب مصر، ورآهم يعبدون الأوثان جمع بنيه ووصاهم

JISHUMI:v1p601/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r6.speaker: عطاء
JISHUMI:v1p601/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says God gave Jacob a choice between life and death, after which Jacob assembled his children and grandchildren and asked whom they would worship.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r6.anchor: وعن عطاء خيره الله تعالى بين الموت والحياة، فجمع ولده وولد ولده، وقال لهم: قد حضر أجلي

JISHUMI:v1p601/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r7.claim: The sons’ concise answer omits a description of the deity to reassure Jacob and signal they follow his and his ancestors’ way; they name Abraham first, then elder son Ismāʿīl, then Isḥāq.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r7.anchor: وإنما أضاف، ولم يصف المعبود بصفته؛ لأنه أوجز وأدل، وأقرب إلى سكون نفس يعقوب

JISHUMI:v1p601/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r8.claim: Being Muslims to the one God means submitting, humbling themselves, affirming His unity, worshipping and obeying Him.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r8.anchor: إلها واحدا ونحن له مسلمون منقادون خاضعون، والمراد نوحده ونعبده ونطيعه

JISHUMI:v1p601/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r9.claim: God is known through His acts: calling Him the God of Jacob and his ancestors implies that He created them all; saying He is one shows He is the creator of all.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r9.anchor: الآية تدل على أنه تعالى يعرف بأفعاله؛ لذلك قال: وإله آبائك كأنه قال: خالقك، وخالق آبائك

JISHUMI:v1p601/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p601/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p601/r10.claim: Grandfathers and uncles may both be called fathers by broad usage; some Ḥanafīs use this verse to treat the paternal grandfather as a father who excludes siblings from inheritance.
JISHUMI:v1p601/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن الجد يسمي أبا، وكذلك العم، وهو فيهما توسع، ولذلك يقال لمن فقد أباه
